Don’t leave me here all alone...!”

Aura was laid to rest
in the casket of glass
I’d had made for her.
Her corpse remains the same
as the day she died.
All because...I wished
not to be left alone in this world...

I saw my face reflected in the glass.
Why do I look like I’m about to cry...?
Why...am I the only one left alive...?!

...Yeah...
This must be my punishment...
My punishment for not being able
to protect Aura, and for denying her
a peaceful rest...
I’ll accept the hand fate’s dealt me...
This time, I’ll fend off all who try
to take Aura.
Until the day I breathe my last...

I warded off all who came
to disturb Aura thereafter.
Until the day I pointed my blade
at yet another approaching figure
in need of a lesson...

“I-I came to leave
some flowers for her!”

Flowers...?
Anyone who’s ever shown their face here
has tried to steal Aura away.
But, this girl is different...
Seeing the bundle of wildflowers
in the girl’s hands,
I felt tears stream down my cheeks.

The girl who came
to leave flowers for Aura
was the very one who had once wished
for her ailing grandmother to be cured.

“My grandmother died,
but I haven’t been able to cry at all...
I’m a horrible grandchild, aren’t I...”

The girl’s teary expression felt familiar.
It was just like my face...
reflected in the casket’s icy glass...

“But, you look like you’re
on the verge of tears as we speak.”
“I...do...?”

Once my words had sunk in,
the floodgates opened,
and the girl broke into heaving sobs.

When she had wept every last tear,
the girl—Tillie—
set her bundle of wildflowers
atop Aura’s casket.
The sight gave me a sense of peace,
and for the first time in ages,
I let down my guard...

So much so,
I didn’t notice the group of humans
closing in on Tillie from behind...

...! Tillie, how could you be so reckless...!
Letting yourself get hurt,
just to protect Aura...!

At this rate, Tillie will...!
Why is it always the kindest souls
that get hurt?!
Aura and this girl are the last people
who deserve to die!
So, please...!

Suddenly, golden light shot out
from the glass casket, covering Tillie.
Don’t tell me...
The light that had enveloped Tillie
then circled around me...
before finally dissipating into the sky.

When Tillie opened her eyes,
she muttered Aura’s name...
Just as I thought...
I closed my eyes
before the empty casket.
Aura is now free...and with her gone,
my reason for living is also—

“Would you like to travel
the world with me?”

Opening my eyes once more,
Tillie was there,
extending her hand up to me.
Ahh... It’s just like back then.
When I met Aura for the first time...

Sorry, Aura.
I’m going to try living a little longer.
Just like with you, I’m going to do
everything I can to protect this girl
who reached out to me.

When everything is over,
I’ll come join you.
So please,
just wait a little longer for me...

Any witches found in human territory
are to be executed on sight.
That’s just how things work in this town—
no, this world.

Mom and Dad always tried
to hide the truth about me...
But, one day, the townspeople found out.
They killed my parents mercilessly, saying,
“Anyone hiding a witch will be tried as one.”

They were going to kill me next.
But, just as I was about to be executed...
she appeared—my savior,
my queen, Miss Lucille...!

“Don’t you dare harm one of my own!”

That’s what Miss Lucille said
as she rescued me
from the town’s Witch Hunt.
As I gazed up at my hero, I thought...

For the rest of my life,
I’ll follow this person...
My leader...!

Led by Leader Lucille,
I was taken to a particular church.
There, a lone nun was caring
for a group of orphans...
Both witches and humans alike,
without prejudice...

The ones leading the orphans
were Leader Lucille and Nebra.
The two did everything together.
But, since Nebra was always saying
that witches and humans
could one day live in harmony,
I struggled to get along with her...

As we spent more time together, though,
I did start to open my eyes
to her way of thinking a little...
Until the day the nun was killed, that is.

It was the same as
what happened to Mom and Dad.
All because that nun thought
witches and humans
could somehow live side by side...!

After that, the children
of the orphanage broke apart.
They split into two groups—
witches and humans—
with both doing everything separately...

I guess witches and humans
can’t live together after all.
Then...

“Witches should just live
with other witches...”

Ah...! I shouldn’t have said that...!

“Good idea.”

Huh? Leader Lucille...what did you just...

“Humans should live with humans,
and witches with witches.
Now come—let’s save witches
from the clutches of those humans
once and for all!”

With those words, Leader Lucille
wasn’t just my leader anymore.
She became everyone’s—
the leader of all witches.

But, Nebra opposed Leader Lucille
until the bitter end,
when their fighting finally led them
to cut ties completely...
I just couldn’t help but feel
like I was the one
who tore them apart...

I still can’t forget the loneliness
in Nebra’s eyes that day...
Years have passed since then,
but the sight only continues
to cast a shadow over my heart.

Leader Lucille also bears
a dark expression on her face
more often than not...

I know I can never be
a replacement for Nebra.
But...!

Am I really...not enough...?

One day, things took a turn.
Nebra appeared,
wanting to speak to Leader Lucille.
She said she’d come to discuss
a peace agreement,
to stop the conflict
between witches and humans...

Leader Lucille was obviously
opposed to any such talks.
But, as she debated
back and forth with Nebra,
she seemed to be having so much fun...

I guess Nebra really is
the only one fit to stand beside
Leader Lucille after all...

After more pushing, Leader Lucille
finally accepted Nebra’s proposal.
I was a bit taken aback,
but I’d always followed Leader Lucille.
Whatever she believes best
is what I believe, too.

Besides, I’m not fit to stand
by Leader Lucille’s side, anyway.
So...this is how things should be...

“Pola, take care of things while I’m gone.”

That’s what Leader Lucille told me,
before she headed to where Nebra
was waiting to make peace talks.
But, it was a location humans
had picked out...

No, I can’t think like this!
I already decided
I’d believe in Leader Lucille, didn’t I?!

If this’s what Leader Lucille’s chosen,
it has to be right.
But then...why do I feel so uneasy...?

I’m probably just anxious
because Leader Lucille’s not here.
It’s still only been two days since she left...
I guess I really am nothing without her...

“Help!!”

What...?
Is something happening outside the gate?

Hesitantly peeking at the commotion,
I saw murky bubbles floating in the air,
engulfing whatever they landed on.
The forest, the town...even the people...
Everything they touched
began to melt away...

What...are these things...?

Ominous bubbles surrounded
the nearby buildings,
swallowing all they latched on to.
It was only a matter of time
before we would also be...

Just then, I heard another cry for help
outside the gate.
Is that...a human’s voice...?

At a time like this,
it shouldn’t matter
if they’re human or witch...
But...!

“Why did this have to happen
while Leader Lucille’s away?!
What should we do...?”

I overheard those words
suddenly slip from another witch.

That’s right...
Up until now, we’ve always relied on
Leader Lucille to decide everything for us.
Just blindly following...
That’s why she...!

I-I have to be the one to make a choice...
since Leader Lucille left me in charge...

But, if I were to make the wrong choice,
and put everyone in danger...

I’m afraid...to choose...!

I never knew how terrifying it was
to make a choice like this...
We’ve always pushed
these kinds of fears on to Leader Lucille...

I’m sorry...for only ever
depending on you this whole time...

But, I still...want to be your friend...!
That’s why...!

“Let’s save them!”

In a trembling voice,
I shouted my choice to the other witches.

“Leaving them to die
just because they’re humans...
That’d make us no different
from those witch hunters!”

In response to my outburst,
a witch anxiously asked,
“But, what would Leader Lucille think?”

“Leader Lucille isn’t here,
so this’s our choice to make!
If we just sit back and do nothing...
then we don’t deserve to call ourselves
her friends!”

With shaking legs, I head for the gate.
I don’t know if what I’m doing is right...
But, I’m just gonna follow
what my heart’s telling me...!

Even if I can’t be the one
standing by your side,
I at least want to hold my head up high...
as your friend...!

“B-Burn.”

As I uttered this,
a blazing pillar of fire pierced the sky...
only to extinguish before my eyes.
Hah...another failure.

I harness the power of words.
Whatever I say becomes reality.
If I say, “Burn,” a fire erupts.
If I say, “Freeze,” there’ll be a blizzard.

The other villagers were
overjoyed to discover my power.
“To conjure anything and
bend reality to your will...
Your potential is limitless,” they said.

But, I couldn’t control it...
Even if I imagined a small campfire,
I would summon an overwhelming blaze.

Any useful power becomes useless
unless you can master it.
If anything, one as boundless as mine
only becomes a looming threat.

...Maybe I should just keep quiet
like the others say.

I messed up again today.

Down in the dumps,
I wandered aimlessly
until I felt a firm clasp on my shoulder.
The only person who’d do that is...

“How’s it going, Potpourri?”

I was right! It was Teacher...!

She was usually busy
teaching the other children,
but she still made time to talk to me.
But...

She’s a little—
no, a really strange person.
I’ve failed so many times,
yet she still treats me kindly...

“Hey, cheer up!
What’s with the long face?”

“I believe in you.
So, you can do it!”

There it is again...
her misplaced faith in me.
She really is strange.

On a day like any other,
Teacher said this to me.

“Potpourri, you can do anything
you set your mind to.
You just need some more confidence...
or maybe try lightening up a little?”

That stung a bit...but she wasn’t wrong.

“All you need is the courage
to believe in yourself.
Why not give it a whirl while thinking,
‘I can do this!’?”

Easier said than done...
I’m still scared of my power.
How could I ever believe in myself...?

It was then that she placed
her hat on my head.

“Here. This is a magic hat.
With this on, you’ll be practically bursting
with extra courage and confidence!”

A magic hat?
I was too old to believe
in things like that anymore.
But...I’d never received a gift before.

“Th-Thank you very much, Teacher.”

It’d been so long
since I’d spoken to anyone...
my voice was trembling.

My teacher really
was telling the truth.

When I wear the hat,
it’s like she’s right there beside me...
Almost as if my nerves are melting away.
Not all of them,
but I do feel like
some weight’s being lifted.

Well, it’s not like I’d ever tell her...
I mean, she’d never let me
live it down if I did.

But one day,
when I’m able to master my magic...
I’d like to thank her properly.

Right as I was getting lost in my thoughts,
I heard shouts outside my house.
What was going on?

Fearfully creaking the door open,
I saw armor-clad humans fighting witches.
Screams and curses echoed
throughout the air,
as if our village had become a battlefield...

I knew I had to run,
but my body was frozen.
Someone, anyone...!

“Potpourri, are you there?!”

Did someone actually come to help me...?

Scrambling into my house,
one of the other witches
locked eyes with me and pleaded.

“Quickly, wipe out the humans
with your power.
The village is in your hands now.”

Stepping outside,
at least a dozen villagers
and humans alike were sprawled
across the ground, unmoving.
A-At this rate, we’ll all be...

I-I have to act now...!
But, can I actually do anything?
All of my previous attempts
to use my power have failed.
What if I end up hurting everyone...?

“It’s alright, Potpourri.”

Teacher...
I felt her warm embrace
and my worries began to fade away.

“You don’t have to fight.
You’re fine the way you are.
Stay kind...”

But then, there was
a sudden flash of light from afar...

“Potpourri, watch out!”

She pushed me away,
and a gunshot rang out behind me...
Teacher...?

I slowly forced myself to turn and look,
only to see her slumped on the floor.

...I-It’s all my fault.
All because I didn’t use my power...!

“Teacher...!
No, please don’t go, not now!”

Her labored breaths
grew more and more shallow...

“Potpourri, you can...”

With the last of her strength,
she placed her hand on my cheek.
She whispered in my ear
as her eyelids slowly fluttered shut.

The brim of my hat
suddenly slumped over my eyes,
as if it was telling me not to look
if I couldn’t bear to.
Maybe it would’ve been easier that way.

But, my teacher’s words
kept ringing in my head.
“Stand up.”

“Believe in yourself...
Have the courage...to believe...”

I gently reached for my hat.
The magic hat
that always gave me strength.
My precious treasure filled
with my teacher’s hopes for me...
Please, lend me your power once more.

Pulling my hat down, I took a deep breath.

I’d never once succeeded
in taming my power,
and I might just fail again.
But, my teacher told me...
to believe in myself. So I...!

I’ll believe in myself!

“Blow them away!”

A small tornado
descended onto the village,
taking only the humans
as it blustered off.

I...I really did it?

Didn’t I tell you?
You can do anything
you set your mind to, Potpourri.

“Teacher...?”

Thinking I heard her voice,
I turned, but no one was there.
She just lay quietly,
growing colder by the second.

If only I had acted quicker...
she could still be alive right now...!
But I know...
I can’t just wallow in my tears forever.
If I did that, she’d only worry more...
and be unable to rest.

“Thank you,
for always having faith in me...
Because of you,
I’m now able to believe in myself.”

I’m still weak,
and I’m sure there’ll be times
when I falter again.
But, I hope you’ll continue
to watch over me
so I can keep my chin up, Teacher...

Plans to create artificial witches
were promptly brought to an end
when one of the experimental subjects
lost control.
The laboratory was destroyed,
and the chief researcher had died.
The project was quickly
shut down thereafter.
However, some of the researchers
had made off with some leftover materials.

Apparently, in a previous experiment,
they tried to make a heartless puppet
feel “despair.”
And so, the “experiments” continued anew,
following the same approach.

Flesh was stripped.
Bones, cracked and pried open.
Every last nerve, scraped out.

When there was nothing left to break,
the body was regenerated,
only to be torn apart again.

After enduring endless, agonizing pain,
the light slowly faded
from the puppet’s eyes.
And in place of that dark void,
new emotions welled up within.

Despair and...hatred...

After awakening my latent magical powers,
reducing the laboratory to rubble
was a simple feat.

I subjected every researcher
scurrying for their lives
to the same “experiments” I was.
Soon, every wriggling worm
was left limp and lifeless.

Such fragile and foolish creatures.
To think I was created to kill these things.
Well, no matter.
I’d be damned to live out
the rest of my life as a weapon.
Besides, I had more important things to do.

Fragments of an untamed Curse
are stirring within me.
Through that very Curse, I can feel it.
My one and only family.
Stronger than any blood bond,
it’s the Curse that connects me to her.

“My dear sister.”

I’m coming to see you now.

When I finally met my big sister,
she was different from what I’d imagined.
Her appearance was that of a young girl,
with limbs so thin and frail.
Her body looked like it would fall apart
at any moment...

“You’re...my little sister?”

She tilted her head,
eyes remaining expressionless.

Yes, dear sister.
We are but imitations of life
created by those foolish humans.
Since our lives are sure to end soon,
what shall we do in our last moments?
Why not exact revenge on humanity?
We could start here, with this land—

Huh...? Go to...school?
A human one? Why?!

To make...memories, you say?
Why should we do
something so human?

Mother Mertillier told us this.

“Homunculi who have become witches
usually live for about a year.
Maybe three years at most.
That’s why I want you to live out
the rest of your time like a normal girl,
Little A.”

The human school was horribly boring.

The underdeveloped human children
were constantly engrossed
in their inane babble or petty quarrels,
sometimes erupting in shrill laughter.
It all seemed like nothing more
than a baffling experiment to me.

Whenever I caught a glimpse
of my sister in the halls,
she was always by Mother’s side.
Seeing that each time
made my heart ache
harder and harder...

Mother had told us
to live like normal girls.
But I’m man-made.
Nothing about my memories, my heart,
or even my sense of time is normal.

As long as I could
stay with my big sister,
I was content...

And so, I played along
with the human charade and went to school.
Day in and day out, I sat at my desk,
stared at the chalkboard,
and said what I needed to say.
It was all so pointless.

My big sister and mother most likely
have less time left than I can imagine.
As each precious day passed,
the feeling that everything was meaningless
kept welling up inside me,
until it was almost enough to burst.

As I gazed listlessly
at the rays of light passing by,
shining through the classroom window...
something within me snapped.

“Don’t you think we could be doing
so much more right now, dear sister?!
I mean...because soon...you’re going to...!”

My voice was shaking.
My vision grew hazy.
Before I could stop myself,
I’d fled from the classroom.
I didn’t know where I was going,
or what I was even running from.
Even so, I couldn’t stop.

As I continued to run,
faint footsteps soon followed after me.

“Leave me alone!”

My hoarse shout sounded
almost like a rusted machine’s wails.

“Take care of yourself
more than you do for me!
Go out and live!”

Once the gears keeping me together
rattled and came apart,
all the words I’d held inside
kept spilling forth.

“Love me more than you love Mother!
Why can’t you live longer?!
Live and die together with me!
Don’t leave me alone...!”

Then, as if to keep me
from crumbling altogether,
I felt two thin arms wrap around me.

“It’s okay, I won’t die.”

Unbelievably, that mechanical,
artificially warm voice stirred a spirit
within me that shouldn’t have existed.

“Because I’m your big sister.”
“Why are you saying something
a human would say...?”

Tears kept welling up,
and they wouldn’t stop.
Though my sister always looked
so small and frail,
she now seemed
so much bigger than before.
It was all too much for me.

“Waaaaah!
Nooo... I don’t want...
I don’t want you to diiiie!”

As I sobbed and heaved,
her small hands kept
gently patting my head.

“Urrrgh...”

I had fallen asleep in the school hallway,
exhausted from my embarrassing
little meltdown.
Slowly, I woke up,
still cradled in my sister’s arms.

“You’re awake? Let’s go home.”
“U-Um...I...”

While I was fumbling over my words,
the smallest, ever so tiniest hint of a smile
tugged at A.A.’s lips.

“I’m your big sister, okay?”

I couldn’t fight against those words.

“...Okay.”

She took me by the hand
and led us back through the city,
now bathed in an orange glow.
I held her small, delicate, yet warm hand—
so fragile that I hesitated
to squeeze it back.
Then slowly,
as if summoning my own resolve,
I tightened my grip.

Mother did say that the Qlipha Project
bestowed A.A. with an angel’s powers,
which granted her life.
And now, her power as a witch
was keeping her alive.

A witch’s power comes from the heart.
I still don’t really understand
what that means,
but I’ll get to the bottom of it one day.
Because it’s the only way
I can hope to save my dear sister.

The light shining in from the windows
lining the school halls appeared a bit dim.
I rubbed my eyes,
hoping to alleviate
my deteriorating optical function.
Walking by her side,
I noticed my little sister,
D.D.’s, brows furrowing.
I know that face.
It is the expression she makes
when she is worried.

“The slowing of my body’s physical functions
are still within the expected range.
There’s no need to worry.”

D.D. froze in place.
It seemed I had only
made her worry more.

“All life has to come to an end one day.
It is just another part of nature.”

“No,” said my little sister,
her eyes downcast as her voice trembled.
“You promised, everything would be okay.”
She was right, I did say that.
But how could I not,
seeing her cry like that? Even so...

I have rust inside me...
This cursed power,
bestowed upon me by the professor,
is why I am still alive.
With each day,
a little more of the rust disappears.
This is the cause of
my physical deterioration.

At this rate,
my heart will most likely
stop after a month.

D.D. tried her best to save me.

“Dear sister, what is your dream?”

Apparently, when a human has a dream,
they are able to exert extra energy
in order to achieve it.
I know what a dream is.
It is another word for a goal.
I thought about it for a while,
then answered, “Nothing.”
At the time,
I had nothing I wished to achieve.

A few days later,
I learned about shooting stars at school,
and was shocked to hear
stars could fall from the sky.
I had looked up at the sky countless times,
but could not believe there was still so much
I did not know about it.

“That’s it,” my sister exclaimed.
“We’ll go look for shooting stars.
Discovering the secrets
of the stars and the sky...
that will be your dream.”

My...dream...

We made a promise
to go stargazing in one month.
So, I would have to keep living until then.
In order...to watch the stars together with her.

My body, having lost its rust,
was being held together
by my power as a witch.
A witch’s power comes from the heart.
For a puppet like me to gain such power...

“Professor. D.D.
Would you like to
research stars with me?”

Before, I had made a promise
with the professor to go see the sky.
I still remember my excitement
from that day.

The three of us headed to the library
and researched all we could
about shooting stars.

D.D. looked up the optimal times
and places to view stars,
while I took notes
about their changing light and colors.
All the while,
the professor drew up sketches
of shooting stars.

“If you wish upon a shooting star,
your wish will come true, you know?”

The professor told me so.
I added what she said to my notes,
and with that,
our observation journal was complete.
“Why can’t it be
next month already?” said D.D.
It seemed even my sister
couldn’t contain her “enthusiasm.”

Even I caught myself smiling in anticipation.

On the day we promised to see the stars,
I looked out of the window
and watched the pouring rain.
Today’s plans would most likely be cancelled.
It was a shame we would not be able
to see the shooting stars,
but seeing my little sister so disappointed
left even more of a pang in my chest.

On the table lay the journal
we had made together,
alongside our coats, scarves,
and warm drinks.

Without thinking, I found myself
on the rooftop of my lord’s mansion.
Maybe the sky will clear up soon,
I thought, and began to get ready
while being soaked by the rain.

“Dear sister,
what in the world are you doing?!
You’re chilled to the bone...!”

D.D. approached me and reached out,
gasping at the cold touch.

“It’s alright.
My thermoregulatory function is just...”

I began to explain,
but realized that was not
what she needed to hear.

“I wanted to go stargazing with you.”

D.D.’s eyes widened,
and tears flowed down her cheeks.
From the sky, a thin ray of light
slowly enveloped us.
Slowly, and quietly, the rain began to stop.

The rain subsided after about an hour.
It was just a simple
meteorological phenomenon,
but the professor appeared overjoyed.
Still recovering from the cold,
my physical functions rapidly deteriorated.
I felt a rising fever, and my vision blurred
as I struggled to walk.

I slumped back in a chair,
gazing listlessly at the sky.
Sitting next to me,
my little sister draped a coat
over my shoulders,
and the professor
handed me a warm drink.

“Little A, are you okay?”
“...Yes, I’m fine.”

For the first time in my life,
I lied to the professor.

Soon it was time,
and the three of us
looked up at the sky.
We marveled at the
astronomical phenomenon
of stars falling from the heavens.
While the two of them
chattered in awe,
I rubbed my eyes once more.

My vision continued to blur.
And after a while, I could not see a thing.

That was the trigger.
My body fell limp and tumbled from the chair.

I was able to see
shooting stars with them both.
With that wish granted,
the last of the rust within me dissipated,
leaving me with only
a final, fulfilling warmth.
I felt someone lift my unmoving body.
From what little I could gather
through my blurred sight,
I saw a single sliver of light
shooting across the sky.

“If you wish upon a shooting star,
your wish will come true...”

My wishes. My dreams.
I thought I didn’t have any,
but they all began to well up,
one after another.

I want to see the sky.
I want to see the stars.
I want to make more
delicious meals for the professor.
I want to keep going to school with D.D.
I want to read more books.
I want to play more.

I want... I want... I want...!

“...to live!
I want to spend more time...
with D.D....and the professor...”

In the distance,
I could hear faint shouts.
But, everything had already
become a blur to me.
As my consciousness
slowly faded to black,
a single ray of light trickled down
towards me like a teardrop.

I awoke amidst countless shining streams,
beckoning me to ascend to the heavens.
Entranced by the light’s warmth,
I felt as though I were melting into it.
I only stopped when I heard
someone call out.

A shooting star flew before me,
fading away as it led me back to the ground.
I could hear my own voice
echoing inside my head,
“It’s okay.”

My eyes shot open, and I was lying in bed.
My blurred vision regained its clarity,
and there seemed to be no abnormalities
with my bodily functions.

Next to my weeping sister,
the professor seemed close to tears herself.
“Looks like your wish was granted,”
she managed to get out.
“You know, only humans
tend to wish upon shooting stars.”

“...Yes. I want to live together with you both,
for as long as I can.”

Honestly, I don’t know
how much more time I have left to live.
But it’s alright.
I’m sure the time I will be able
to spend with the two of them
shall protect me until the end.

Today’s the day I’ve waited so long for—
the Flower Festival!
There’s no better day of the year
for making friends than this!
But, since I’ve always been too sickly
to even go to school,
I’ve spent most of my days
all alone in my room.

“Yesterday was so much fun, wasn’t it?”
“What should we do today?”
“See you tomorrow!”
All I’ve ever wanted was someone
to share those words with—a friend.
I wanted a friend so bad,
I even kept chugging down
that bitter, icky medicine this whole time!

Now, it’s time to head for that festival!
...Wait, what’s a girl doing
collapsed in front of my house?!

The girl had lost all of her memories,
so we decided to let her stay with us
for the time being.
She didn’t know her own name,
or where she lived.
Even my mother said
she’d never seen a girl so beautiful before.

The girl’s eyes were the color
of when sunset meets night,
and they were so pretty
I could hardly look away.
Inspired by a tulip of the same color,
I decided to call her Grita.

Even after night fell,
Grita still seemed nervous.
What could I do to cheer her up...?
...Ah!

“Want to go to the Flower Festival
with me tomorrow?
There’ll be loads of people and flowers,
so they say it’s a must-see event!”

After thinking for a moment,
Grita gave a small nod.
She still seems a bit uncomfortable,
but I hope that soon,
she’ll be able to smile again!

Since Grita arrived,
a month’s blown by in a flash!
My health’s even been so good,
it’s practically a miracle!
So, the two of us
have been going out to play every day.

We’ve weaved flower crowns,
watched shooting stars,
and I’m pretty sure we even
took a nap together one day after lunch!

“They’re finally done!”

What we’d finished
were two flower reliefs
Grita and I had been carving.
We both decided to slowly carve
the flower we’d liked the most
at the Flower Festival,
wanting to recreate it somehow.

“Your flower turned out cute, Lumica.
Even if it is a little rough
around the edges.”
“I could say the same about yours,
you know!”

For some reason, it was so funny,
we looked at each other
and burst out into laughter.

“Let’s be friends forever, Grita!”
“Yeah. It’s a promise.”

Grita held out her pinky finger,
which I hooked my own around.

“Let’s be together forever...!”

“Let’s head down to the lake today...
Wait, is something wrong, Grita?”
“I can’t stay with you anymore, Lumica.”

Grita’s voice was much colder than usual...

“Wh-Why not? You can tell me anything!
We’re friends, aren’t we?”
“...Not anymore...”

“Wait, Grita...!”
I have to chase after her.
But, my legs won’t move...!

Did I do something to make her mad...?
If I did, I guess it only makes sense
she’d feel that way...
Even to the point
of not being my friend anymore...

...! If I did something wrong,
then I need to apologize...
I don’t want to quit being friends...
Even if I can’t make her come back,
I want to give her a proper goodbye...!

I hurried outside.
I wonder where she went...?
As I hesitated, I heard a distant scream.
Running in the direction of the sound,
I saw Grita being attacked
by a cursed creature!

I jumped in front of the creature
without a second thought.
Its sharp claws dug deep into my skin.
...It hurts...!
I don’t care what happens to me...but...!

“I won’t let you hurt my best friend!”

The moment the words left my lips...
the cursed creature went flying.

“Thank goodness...I was able to protect you...
Grita...are you hurt anywhere...?”

“Lumica...! Your wounds are so deep...
I said all those horrible things to you,
so why did you shield me like that?!”

“Because...you’re my friend...”

“...! At this rate, you’ll...!
No... There is one way...
...With this, it really will be goodbye...”

“Gri...ta...?”

“Let the light
of this life I cannot lose shine anew.
If thou desires the light thou has given me
in exchange, then...”

Ahh... This light is so bright, I can’t see a...
Huh...? Where...? Oh... Right...
I got injured, and then...
But, it doesn’t hurt.
Oh yeah, Grita—

I realized I was in Grita’s arms.
Two white wings sprouted from her back...
and a ring of light floated above her head.
She looked just like...

“...An angel...?”

Grita told me everything.

About how she really was an angel.
That she’d fought and lost to a demon.
And that she’d lost her memories
from the impact of crashing to the ground.
She even told me that I’d accidentally
enacted a miracle.

“Us angels have the power
to grant the wishes of humans.
When you wished to save me,
the power of the miracle
lying dormant inside me reacted,
and it enacted a miracle
that drove off the cursed creature.”

“Miracles require giving up
something as big as the wish in exchange—
something precious to the one enacting it.
For you, Lumica...
it’ll likely be one day’s worth of memories
with the person you hold most dear.”

“I-If it was to save you, Grita,
forgetting one day is nothing!
We can just make even more
fun memories in the future!”

“Yeah. That’s...what I wanted for us, too...”

Grita averted her eyes.
That’s when I noticed...
that Grita was slowly fading away.

“This was the only way
to save you from certain death, Lumica.
We exist to grant wishes.
It is forbidden for us to grant our own.
So...”

“...No... That’s not what I want...!
God, please!
Take back Grita’s wish!
Only save Grita...!”

“I can’t let that happen.
Because, a world without you,
is a world I can’t love.”

As Grita said so,
she flashed the prettiest smile I’d ever seen.

“I’m glad I was able to see you in the end.
Goodbye, Lumica...
You’ll always be my best friend...”

Just as I tried to put my arms
around Grita’s fading body...
she transformed into specks of light.
All that remained was a single feather.
I picked it up and grasped it tightly.

The time you and I spent together
was the happiest I’ve ever been.
Thanks...for being my friend...
Thank you...for coming into my life...!
You’ll forever be...my very best friend, Grita...!

Phwaaah...! What a good nap...
Wait, why am I sleeping outside?!
And it’s sunset already?!
But, I was planning on going to the lake
with Grita today!

Grita...hmm...isn’t here...
Did she go off somewhere
trying to look for me, or something?
Huh...? I’m holding something...
Is this...a feather?
...Ah...!

Blown off by the wind,
the feather turned into a speck of light,
then twinkled and disappeared...
How pretty...

Why...does my chest feel so tight, it hurts...?
Am I sad that I didn’t get to go
to the lake with Grita...?
This is weird...
We could go tomorrow, or the day after that,
or really any time at all...
So, why...?
Suddenly, tears began to stream
down my cheeks.

I don’t know why I’m crying, but...
Yeah... I’ll just let myself cry a while.
Because, it feels like I should.

Yesterday was so fun, wasn’t it?
Today...is coming to an end,
so let’s try again tomorrow!

And just like that,
we’ll keep being friends forever, Grita...!

“Find that witch!”

The people from the Inquisition
ran down the main street,
off into the distance.
Till their footsteps grew faint,
I couldn’t stop shakin’.

Ever since I awakened as a witch,
this is how I’ve spent my days...
Get found, then run.
Rinse an’ repeat.

How long will this go on...?
Where...should I even run to...?
If life was gonna be like this,
I should never’ve even been...!

But, just then,
I heard roars of laughter
comin’ from somewhere nearby.

It was the kinda laughter with the warmth
that could lift even the lowest of spirits.

The only places witches can safely survive
are the darkest of back alleys.
But...

Feelin’ as if that laughter was callin’ my name,
I stepped out into the light.

In the middle of the busy street,
a travelin’ gunslinger was puttin’ on a show.

It looked like a blast...

The girl’s smile drew people to her
like moths to a flame.
You could just tell how much she wanted
to entertain everybody passin’ by...

I took one step, and then another,
as if she was drawin’ me in, too.

“Well, looks like some more guests
have joined us,
so let’s kick off another round!”

Spinnin’ and jugglin’ her two pistols with ease,
the girl caught the eye of everyone
who’d gathered there.
Even passersby stopped in their tracks
just to watch her.

Ah...! What should I do...?

Before I knew it,
I’d walked all the way up to the front...
Even worse,
I’d done it while lookin’ this scruffy...

Just as I was about to make my way back,
I saw a hand outstretched before me.

“Hey, you!
Help me out a little, will ya?”

“Huh? Me?!
Um, but I can’t do any tricks...!”

“Don’t worry, anybody can do it!
All you gotta do is throw me a ball, see?”

The gunslinger passed me the ball in question,
then stepped back a little.

Urgh... I’m not so sure I can do this...

B-But, if it’s only throwin’ a ball...
Yah...!

When I threw the ball,
it ended up hurtlin’ right towards the crowd...
Ahh... I just knew I’d mess up...

But, the very next moment,
the girl spun through the air,
and shot the ball clean through the middle.

Her bullseye sent a shower of
colored confetti down on the heads
of the onlookers...
Then, a round of applause
an’ laughter rang out.

“Nice work!
Thanks to you, that trick was a huge success!”

Thanks to me...?
But, I messed the whole thing up...

Just as I hung my head in shame,
the travelin’ gunslinger pushed me forward.

“Now, give another big round of applause
for my tiny assistant here!”

“U-Um, but, I didn’t...”

“What’re you saying?
Thanks to you,
everybody had a great time, didn’t they?
Just take a look for yourself!”

Lookin’ out at the crowd,
everyone was clappin’
with big smiles on their faces.
All for a scruffy lookin’ girl like me...

It made me so happy,
I felt myself break into a smile.

“You probably have a knack
for making people smile, y’know.
I mean, just look
at what a great smile you’ve got!”

“Alright, I can’t let you take all the spotlight.
Gather ’round, ’cause the world’s
greatest gunslinger Cordie’s show
is far from over!”

That was my fated meetin’
with the great Cordie.

From that day on,
I wandered the world
as a travelin’ gunslinger myself.

It didn’t change the fact
that I was spendin’ my days runnin’
from the Inquisition.
But unlike before, every day’s now full of fun!
I have the great Cordie to thank for that, too.

If she hadn’t called out to me back then,
I’d be crouched down in the dark
of those alleys even now.

The great Cordie shone a bright light
on my future.

A half-rate gunslinger like me
still can’t stand on the same stage
as the great Cordie...
But, I’ll practice lots and lots
till I get good enough to perform ’longside her!

I mean, I’m able to pull off stunts now
I couldn’t even dream of doin’ at first.
So, let’s keep this gunsmoke blazin’!

I made it to a new town,
but it feels like everybody here is sorta...
down in the dumps.

Oh yeah...
Not too long ago,
I heard a rumor ’bout a town
where half its people were lost in a disaster...
So that’s why everyone looks so sad...

Alright then,
I’ll give everyone a reason to smile again!
Just like the great Cordie did for me!

“How d’you do, folks?
Now gather...’round...”

H...Huh...?
Not only is nobody comin’ up to me...
nobody’s even turned their head to look.

In that case,
I’ll reel em’ in with a pop of color
from one of my rainbow bullets!

N-Not even a glance, huh?
Maybe if I send ’em flowers
carried by balloons...
That didn’t work, neither...
Th-Then, I’ll use my special ball to...

But, just as I went to grab it,
my tremblin’ hands
dropped the ball to the ground.
It rolled a ways
before gettin’ crushed underfoot,
its confetti surprise spillin’ out for all to see.

“A...Ahaha... Looks like I messed up...”

While gatherin’ all the loose confetti,
I lifted my head to see if anyone was watchin’.
But, nobody paid me the slightest attention...

Guess I’m really no good, after all...
As if I could ever have the power
to make somebody smile...!

Uuu...!
With the crumpled tatters of the confetti
clutched in my fists,
I crouched down on the spot and cried...

I don’t have the power to make people smile...
It only makes sense, I guess.
No matter how much I copy the great Cordie,
it’s not like I can ever be her.

Liftin’ my head after a spell,
I noticed a girl was watchin’ me.
Her eyes had lost any trace of emotion...
just like my eyes had back then...

But, I’ve changed since then...!
After meetin’ the great Cordie,
the once dark world around me
seemed to gain new light.

“You probably have a knack
for making people smile, y’know.”

Heh... I really am just half-rate.

I wasn’t smilin’ one bit.
If I look this unsure of myself,
nobody’s gonna wanna watch.

If I wanna reel ’em in,
I’ve gotta put a smile on my own face first.
’Cause that’s how
the great Cordie’s smile got me!

“Come one, come all!
The travelin’ gunslinger Flack’s show
is about to begin!”

I continued performin’ my show.
Everyone kept on walkin’ past me,
but I made sure to keep a smile on my face
just the same.

But while I performed,
the girl from before walked up to watch me.
Just like I did that day...

“Get ready, ’cause these next tricks
are gonna be even flashier!”

When I shot her a smile,
light returned to her vacant eyes.
And...

Ahh...!
She finally smiled...!

Finally, the moment has arrived.

The heated gaze of the audience,
eagerly waiting for the opening act.
Ah, it sure has been a while since I’ve felt it.

But today, it’s the birth of a brand new me.
Hehe! Because...

“Great Cordie—I mean, Ringmaster!
We’re all hitched up and ready to roll!”

Turning around, I saw Flack
and the rest of our troupemates
waiting for my signal.
Everyone worked really hard for this day,
didn’t they?

“Alright, let’s get this show on the road!
Curtains up for the
Fran Circus Troupe’s first show!
Let’s all have fun today~!

It all started with
a simple question from Chiffon.

“What’s a sir-kus?”

I happened to spot her and Flack
while passing through the courtyard.

Flack sure did her darndest to try and explain,
but it looked like her points
weren’t really getting across.

Hmm~ It is kinda hard to put
that sense of wonder into words.
It’s definitely gotta be experienced firsthand...

But, to think there are kids out there
who don’t know anything about the circus.
In that case...

“We just gotta bring the circus to them!”

Life’s way too short
to not know how fun it is!
So...

“C’mon, Flack!
This marks the beginning
of the Fran Circus Troupe!”

We’ll form a circus troupe right here in Fran.
One that’s even more mesmerizing
and fun-filled than the one back home!

With that decided,
we needed to start
recruiting troupemates right away.
Just me and Flack wouldn’t cut it.

Hmm~ We’ll definitely need music...
Milla can handle that.

And then we’ll need a dancer...
That’s Hathor for sure!

What else, what else...?

I started reaching out to the girls
I had already set my sights on.
Thankfully, everyone seemed down to join~!

We were set to have our first performance
in three days at the city square.
Alright, let’s blow everyone away
with the best show ever!

Hathor’s exotic dance,
accompanied by Milla’s music,
would be the opening act.
Perfect, one down!

Huh? Mimi, you want to dance too?
Sure, sure! We can all dance together!
Let’s see... Then, you’ll go...

Oh? You’ll handle this one, Hathor?

She quickly took charge,
dishing out instructions
and organizing everything in no time.
We sure got lucky,
having someone with lots of experience
behind and on-stage.

If anything, the real issue was...

“You want me to be your assistant,
Great Cordie?!
I can’t do that! No way, no how!”

“Aw, shoot!
Now our whole show’s gonna go up in smoke
’cause of me... Aaaargh!”

Yeah...it’s been pretty much
like this the whole time...

Welp, no biggie.
Looks like it’s up to
Ringmaster Cordie to save the day!

I still remember my first performance.
I was so nervous and worked up,
worrying about what’d happen if I messed up.

But then, the ringmaster and my troupemates
reassured me that I could do it.
They taught me
the most important thing to focus on.

“It’s okay, Flack.
Don’t you worry about messing up.
What matters is how you make the most of it.”

If someone focuses too much
on doing things perfectly,
just for their smile
to be sacrificed in the end,
it’d be such a waste.

What’s important isn’t
pulling stuff off flawlessly,
but having tons of fun on a stage
where everyone’s the star!

“So let’s see that smile, Flack.
And have fun out there!”

A circus isn’t something
that can be pulled off alone.
If even one person is missing,
it just won’t work.

“We’ll put on the best show
only we can provide,
and make those crowds out there smile
’til their cheeks hurt!
I know we can do it together, Flack!
And if the going gets tough,
you’ve got Ringmaster Cordie
right here by your side!
So, that makes you basically invincible!”

I ended with a wink, and Flack finally smiled,
looking more reassured.

“Yes, ma’am!
I’ll follow ya to the ends of the world,
Great Cordie!”

Aw, jeez...
Right now, I’m the Ringmaster, remember?
Well, as long as she’s smiling,
I don’t really mind.

And just like that, the big day arrived!

The square was packed
with all sorts of folks,
children and adults alike.

Oh, Chiffon made it!
Along with Nina and Veela...

And so many people,
all waiting for us with excitement.

Whoo~ Now I’m getting pumped too!

We’ve gotta treat them
to the best show ever—
one so great no one will ever forget it!

“Ringmaster, we’re all set over here!”

I was worried Flack might be nervous,
but she seemed fine...
I mean, how could she not?
Being on stage is so fun!

“Alright! Break a leg, everyone!
Let’s make the Fran Circus Troupe’s
debut performance one for the books!”

The first act was Hathor and Mimi’s dance!
Then came Asahi’s aerial acrobatics show,
followed by Tropon’s juggling!

Using fire and ice,
we put on a show only we could provide,
and the audience was going wild.
Finally, to top things off...

“Let’s close this out, Flack!”

We fired our guns at the same time.
Each bullet collided into another,
splattering paint all over the stage.

But, surely that wasn’t enough
to satisfy the audience, right?

We both leapt into the air.
This was a tough trick that required us
to be in perfect sync to pull off.
But for us, it was easy-peasy!

As we crossed paths mid-air,
we tossed our guns to each other.
Upon landing at the same time,
standing back-to-back... Bang!

A final splash of paint spattered,
completing our beautiful field
of colorful flowers~♪
Amidst the thunderous applause and cheers,
we gracefully took a bow.

“We did it, Flack!”

While we were mid-high-five,
a group of kids from the crowd ran up to us...

“Huh? You guys wanna join the circus too?
Sure, why not? Sounds like fun to me!
C’mon, step right up!”

As soon as I called out to them,
all the kids rushed onto the stage.

It’ll be your first time
being part of a show like this, huh?
Well, there’s nothing to it!
As long as you’re having a blast,
that’s all that counts!

“Gather ’round, everyone!
Let’s have some fun!”

My mother is a wolf.

She found me...a human infant,
with the ears and tail of a wolf...
inside an abandoned house...

Mother brought me home with her,
but the leader of her pack didn’t accept me.
He said the weak are culled.
That is the law of nature,
and is not to be disobeyed.

Mother wouldn’t hear of it,
and left to form a new pack.
Just her and I.

Until we were welcomed in
by a human settlement,
Mother never gave in to
the hardships she was faced with.
She continued to protect
and raise me through it all.

My wish is to be like Mother...
No... I must be strong!

I am not weak.
I will become living proof
that Mother made the right choice.
My strength will serve as my repayment,
and atonement, to her...

I will protect the human pack
that took me and my mother in.
Then, lead them as
the unmoving light of Heaven
guides us from the night sky...
I must become a strong, noble wolf...!

A messenger came to us
from the People of the Stone,
who had long fought us
for control of our land.

Their demand—to hand me over to them...
Hah! Just thinking about it
makes my fur bristle.

They sever trees clear down to their roots,
build giant homes of stone,
needlessly slaughter animals—
as if I would ever heel
before the likes of them!

For now, I captured the messenger
and held a meeting
to decide what to do with her, but...

“I should just kill that messenger girl.
What’s there to hesitate for?”

But, the ones who took us in resisted, saying,
“If anything happens to that girl,
the People of the Stone could use it
as an excuse to invade us.
That’s all the more reason
we should try to remain...diplomatic.”

The People of the Stone
have managed to overtake
the surrounding settlements.
But, even if they outnumber us...

“I don’t care how many of them there are—
I’ll tear them apart with these fangs!”

“But, it’s far too dangerous!
If anything were to happen to you...!”
Why does everyone treat me
as though I’m weak...?

Is this because...I’m only half wolf...?

“Th-This is all just one
big misunderstanding!
I didn’t know that
was what they wanted—really!”

I had barely entered the tent before
the captive messenger girl started prattling off
that frantic apology.
Apparently, the girl was of
the People of the Plains,
but from a tribe that was taken over
by the People of the Stone.
“I’m too weak,
so I had no choice but to obey their will!”—
or so she said.

The messenger was desperately searching
for any way to make it out
of her predicament alive.
The girl’s attempts to beg for her life
were truly a pathetic display to behold.

“Why do you resist?
The weak are destined to die.
It’s the law of nature.”

“‘Law of nature’...?
Do you really think
that just because humans are weaker,
any injustice against us is deserved?”

The girl’s demeanor instantly changed.
Her cowardice from earlier vanished,
an almost fiery defiance flaring up in its place.

“Guess that ‘guardian deity’ shtick
is just a name to you.
In the end, you’re no different
from those people in the city.”

“Don’t you dare lump me in
with those People of the Stone! I’m...!”

What do they know...?!
This girl before me, the People of the Stone,
the ones who took me in...!

Even though I’ve been the one
fending off the People of the Stone’s attacks
this whole time...!
Why does no one
acknowledge me as a wolf...?!

Just what...am I missing...?!

“We wish to speak only
with the chief of your tribe.
We’ll be waiting at the temple
near your settlement.”
That was in the letter sent to me
by the People of the Stone.

My tribe tried to stop me,
but I headed for the meeting place alone.
No wolf, especially my mother,
would ever turn their back
on such a request.

I made it to the temple, but...
what is this smell?
Is something...rotting...?

Just then, a trail of fire rose into the air.
The billowing flames surrounded
the temple’s interior with frightening speed.

So, that rotten stench
was just to cover up
the smell of gunpowder...!

Suddenly, a loud noise rang out behind me.
Whipping back,
I saw one of the temple’s pillars
about to crash down upon me...
But, that very moment,
someone pushed me out of harm’s way.

Mother...why are you here...?!

But, she gave no response to my probing gaze,
as she lied helplessly,
trapped beneath the pillar.

Mother...should be strong...
So, why is she...?
I could hear someone’s
fast-approaching footsteps...
It’s...that messenger girl...?

“What are you spacing out for?!
Do your whole deity thing
and save her, quick...!”

The girl yanked my hand,
but my body was frozen on the spot.

“You’re different from me!
You have the power
to save your mother,
so what are you waiting for?!”

“The weak...are destined to die...
That’s why, I can’t...”

Her hand slapped my cheek.
Why...do you look like you could cry...?

“Then...would your mother abandon you
if you were weak?”

My words caught in my throat.
The sight of my mother
flashed through my mind.
Mother has always...!

“You don’t just abandon
who’s most important to you
just because they’re weak!
You fight like hell to protect them!”

“But, a wolf...should be noble, and strong...”

“You’re half human, aren’t you?!”

“Who cares about looking noble or strong,
just break that stupid law already!
Write your own rules,
like the humans you look down on so much!”

I’d always resented the human part of me.

Whenever I was distraught
over my inability to be like Mother,
she’d gently lick my fur and tell me this...

“You are fine as you are.
We may look different,
but you are still my daughter.”

...! Why didn’t I believe her...?
Even though those words...
were from the heart...!

I ran to Mother’s side
to lift the fallen pillar.
...It moved a little...!
If I just push a little more...!

Nrgh...! The fire’s coming closer...!
Even if my body burns to ash...
I’m going to save you, Mother...!

“Ugh, enough already...!
Get out of your head, and just focus!”

The girl yelled this
while pushing the pillar from beside me.
As she did, a light shot out.

The fire...isn’t hot anymore...?
Has this girl...
been blessed by some kind of spirit...?
Whatever this power may be,
with this, I can...!

I gathered all of my strength,
and shoved the pillar off of Mother.

Once we had escaped
from the burning temple,
I gently let Mother down from my arms.
She gave me a few licks of thanks in return...
Thank goodness...!

What’s this...?
There’s a different scent on the wind...
Wait...it’s smoke coming from the settlement...!

So this was all a plot to kill me off
and attack the settlement, huh...?
If we don’t act fast...!

“Messenger of Flames.
Lend me your power once more!”

“Don’t give me some weird nickname!
I don’t have the power to control fire.
In fact, I...”

The girl’s hands began to tremble.
Did something bad happen to her before?

“You’re the one who just told me
to break nature’s law regardless of how I look.
After lighting this fire within me,
do you really want to go back on your word
so soon?”

After a moment’s hesitation,
the girl slapped both of her cheeks
and looked up at me.
In her eyes blazed the same fire I’d seen there
the day we met.

“That’s what I like to see.
What’s your name, Messenger?”

“...It’s Mihri...”

“Come with me, Mihri.
To escape with our lives,
let’s fight against fate
like the pitiful humans we are...!”

As I gazed down at the village below
from the old castle window,
a maid standing behind me spoke.

“Lady Carmilla, it appears
you skipped your studies again today.”
“...What’s the point of studying, anyway?”

We are a clan of vampires
who drain the life force of those we touch.
We are born from our mothers’ corpses
after stealing their life force
while inside the womb.
Monsters despised even by witches.

“Either way, I’m just going to stay cooped up
in this castle my whole life,
all to hide what I really am.”

The maid didn’t respond to my bitter words.
Instead, she just bowed gracefully
as she always does.

“Your meal is ready.”

Eating normal food fills our stomachs,
but it doesn’t quench our thirst.
Letting out a small sigh,
I glanced down once more at the village below.

Pulling my hood low over my face,
I snuck into the village.
As I made my way
through the bustling crowds,
I pretended to stumble and trip.

“Ah, excuse me...”

With just a brief touch,
the man’s face turned pale,
and he collapsed to the ground.
Panicked murmurs quickly spread
through the crowd.

Sneaking out to drain
life force like this is dangerous,
but it’s the only way we can survive.
As I repeated apologies
over and over in my heart,
I slipped away from the scene.

On my way back,
my thirst became unbearable.
When I reached the forest,
I spotted a small rabbit.

“I’m sorry...”

As I gently picked up the rabbit,
its life faded away instantly in my arms.

“This is the only way we can live...”

Tears rolled down my cheeks,
glowing crimson like blood.

Three days after my meal,
the village was in an uproar.

“My son won’t wake up...!”

To the villagers’ pleas,
an inquisitor responded solemnly.

“This must be the work of vampires.”
“Those creatures in the castle
have stolen his soul!
This village is under attack!”

With each word from the inquisitor,
the frightened villagers began
to arm themselves, one after another.
The fervor spread quickly like a flame,
and soon the entire village
was roaring with anger.

“Burn the castle to the ground!
Kill every last one of that cursed clan!”

All I could do was hide
in a nearby building’s shadow,
holding my trembling body tightly.

“Why...? How can it be that easy for them
to do something so cruel...?”

At that moment,
I wasn’t scared of being caught.
Instead, I was shaking
as the humans screamed like madmen.

...I have to tell everyone back at the castle!
I have to hurry...!

Forcing my shaking legs to move, I ran.

Please, make it in time...!

“Father, something terrible has happened!”

I burst into the grand hall,
where my father looked at me with cold eyes.

“Carmilla. I heard you
skipped out on your studies again.
One day, you’ll lead this clan.
You need to—”

“Now’s not the time to worry about that!
There’s an inquisitor in the village!
They’ve figured out what we are!”

I desperately pointed out the window.
Under the cover of night,
countless flames were moving
through the forest,
making their way toward the castle.
And yet, my father didn’t budge.

“We’ve paid off the Church many times.
This little investigation’s all just for show.
There’s no need to worry.”

Father didn’t understand.
He hadn’t seen the rabid mobs of villagers.
That frenzy couldn’t be stopped
with any more bribes.

What should I do now...?

“Father, there’s still time...
Please, you have to believe me!”

Even as I begged, my father refused to listen.
How can I make him believe me...?

“I can grant that wish of yours.”

Huh? Wh-Who’s there...?!

“Don’t be afraid. I’m on your side.
I also lent my power to your mother before.
You want power too, don’t you?”

I didn’t trust the strange voice
echoing in my head...
But, I was left with no choice
but to make a wish.

“If you’re telling the truth...
then give me the power to save everyone!”
“Hehe, that’s a good girl.”

Something surged into my body,
and an unfamiliar sigil appeared on my skin.

“That’s the mark of our contract.
Proof that you have become my acolyte,
and you have been granted my power.”

Strength flooded through me...
With this, I can—

“Everyone,
believe what I’m saying and run, now!”

My voice, now imbued with power,
echoed through the halls.
My father slowly rose to his feet in response.
Thank goodness! It’s working...!
As relief washed over me,
Father bowed his head towards me.

“As you command, Lady Carmilla.”

F-Father...? Even the maids...
Their faces were pale, like lifeless dolls...

What...is this? What’s going on?!

“Well, what’d you expect?
Just like you wished,
they’re now puppets
who’ll obey your every word.”
“No, this isn’t what I wanted!
Change them back!”

But at that moment,
smoke began to fill the room.
Peering out the window,
I saw the castle was ablaze...

“Don’t lose hope.
There’s still a way out of this.
If you command yourself to save everyone,
you’ll be able to harness power
beyond your limits.”

“Just how far are you...?!”
Everything finally clicked in my head.
This was a demon.
A venomous demon who twists
the hearts of people with sweet temptations.

“Hehe. Suit yourself,
but if you don’t get a move on,
they’re all going to die.”

Why...? Why do the humans,
and now, even demons,
keep coming after us...?
Why do they keep trying
to take everything from us?!

No one’s going to save us...
So... I’ll have to protect everyone myself.
I won’t let anyone take a single thing from us,
ever again...

Don’t think things’ll keep
going your way anymore.
Fate, demons...nothing will stop me!

“Listen up, me.
I need you to become the strongest—
stronger than anyone out there!!”
The sigil from my contract began to glow,
and then...

A month has passed since then.
We’ve started our new life
in a remote country.

Every morning, Father pats my head
while Mother lovingly prepares meals for us.
Then there’s my little brother,
who always begs me to read him books.

Here, we don’t have to worry about villagers
or inquisitors hunting us down.
Every day is peaceful and happy.

Wait a minute...
Didn’t Mother...?
And my brother...?

...No, it doesn’t matter anymore.

“Thanks to the magnificent Carmilla,
everyone’s happy now!”

Yeesh, that’s cold!
...Guess this marks yet another time
I’ve gotten water dumped on me
by these city people.
When will they get it through their thick skulls
that I don’t have the power to make fire?

This was just another day in the life
of a person whose tribe
was taken over by the city.
My new life began the day my settlement
was burned to the ground.

“It will all be alright.”—
Those were the words
my mother repeated to me
as flames raged all around us.
Wrapped in her arms,
all I could do was tremble in fear...
Then, when I came to,
everything and everyone except me
had been burned to ash.

I’m sure that was when
I first awakened to my power
to shield myself from flames.
Nothing turned out “alright” at all...
If this pathetic power
could only save one person,
I’d rather it were...!

Ugh...! Okay, enough thinking!
It’s about time I got the job
that city official threw at me over with!

If I remember right,
he wanted me to bring back a “star”
or something from the People of the Plains...
But, what does “star” even mean...?

I get that a messenger sent
from the enemy’s side
would set people on edge...
But why’d I get captured
just for delivering a message?!

“What’s all this noise?”

Everyone’s bowing to that girl
with the wolf ears and tail...
Is she the kid of some bigwig around here?

“I am a messenger sent from the city...!
I was told to retrieve a ‘star’ from your tribe...”

Wh-Why’s everybody
whispering to each other?
What does “star” even mean?!

“That ‘star’ is code for Yildiz.
They want me.”

Yildiz...? So this Yildiz is the “star?”
In other words, they want her?
Wait, why?

“Oh, come now!
If it was the chief of your tribe I’d understand,
but a kid—”

“I am the chief of this tribe.”

“Come on, you’re joking...!
Hehe... Heh... You...are joking, right...?”

I completely forgot that some tribes
revere animals as their guardian deities...!

So now, I’m a bad guy
trying to take their precious guardian!
Worst case scenario,
they might even sentence me to...!

That slimy city official!!
He knew this would happen, didn’t he?!
I have to plead my case!
If that girl learns the truth,
surely she’ll take pity on me
and undo these restraints—

“Why do you resist?
The weak are destined to die.
It’s the law of nature.”

“‘Law of nature’...?
Do you really think
that just because humans are weaker,
any injustice against us is deserved?”

I might, for only being able to save myself...
But, the rest of my tribe who fought
to protect our land, and my mother,
didn’t deserve to be burned alive...!

The weak are destined to die...?
And that’s just the law of nature...?
Hah...! Get real...!

“Guess that ‘guardian deity’ shtick
is just a name to you.
In the end, you’re no different
from those people in the city.”

“Don’t you dare lump me in
with those People of the Stone!
I’m...!”

Why’s she suddenly so upset?
...Though, that sounds like
more than just anger...
Well, it’s not my problem, either way...

Seems like that wolf girl
resents the human side of her.

Unfortunately for her,
hating oneself is as human as it gets...
Wait, this isn’t the time
to be thinking about this!

I’d been sentenced to imprisonment
under constant surveillance.
And the one charged with watching me
was a wolf—the wolf girl’s mother...
Am I...about to be wolf chow...?

I mean, she’s even licking my wounds!
And when I go to sleep,
she brings me a blanket—
W-Wait... How gracious...!

“You remind me of my parents.
They’re both dead now, though.”

The wolf’s ears perked up.
Seems like she really can
understand human speech...

Feeling strangely at ease,
I found myself telling her all kinds of things.
Like stories about my mother,
my past, my power...

“Miss Wolf?
Why’re you standing all of a sudden—
Gyahhh! Could you not p-p-p-pull
on my sleeve like that?!”

Does she want me to come with her?!
A-And why is she making me run this fast?!

Haah... Haah... Is this...a temple?
It’s on fire, so why is that wolf girl here...
Wait, watch out...!
An explosion sends a pillar flying,
and she’s about to be crushed by it...!

The wolf suddenly darted from my side,
pushing her daughter out of harm’s way...
before getting trapped helplessly
beneath the pillar.

The flames are getting closer...!
W...We have to save
that wolf girl’s mother fast...!

“What are you spacing out for?!
Do your whole deity thing
and save her, quick...!”

The wolf girl wouldn’t move
even when I yanked her hand.
What the hell is her problem?!

“You’re different from me!
You have the power to save your mother,
so what are you waiting for?!”

This girl has the power
to fend off the city soldiers all by herself...
If I’d had that kind of power back then...!

I could have saved my friends,
or countless others...
So, why is she hesitating...?!

“The weak...are destined to die...
That’s why, I can’t...”

Hearing those words,
I slapped her cheek
without a second thought.

“You don’t just abandon
who’s most important to you
just because they’re weak!
You fight like hell to protect them!”

After taking in everything I’d yelled at her,
the girl ran to her mother’s side,
tears in her eyes.
Now, if we can just push that pillar off...!

The flames are almost on us...
Crap, at this rate...!
Nrgh...! I’m scared...!
What should I do?
What do I...?!

“Ugh, enough already...!
Get out of your head, and just focus!”

Just then, something inside me shot out...

“Messenger of Flames.
Lend me your power once more!”

That’s what Yildiz told me after we escaped,
her eyes focused on the smoke
rising from the settlement.

Back in the temple,
all three of us were shielded
from those flames...
Even though my pathetic power
should have only worked on me...

But making a miracle like that happen twice...?
...No, there’s no time for doubt...!
I can’t guarantee anything,
but I still have to try...!

We hurried towards the settlement,
only to find everything
bathed in a vortex of fire.

Torches in hand,
the city soldiers looked on at their handiwork
and laughed.
I can hear cries for help
coming from the flames...!
There are people trapped inside...!
Forcing my buckling legs to move,
I jumped into the fire.

Before me was a lone girl, trembling in fear.
I wrapped her in my arms,
protecting her from the surrounding flames.

I just need to remember
the feeling from earlier...!
Shoot out, now! Quickly...!
...Why isn’t it working?!

It’s impossible after all...!
My power...is useless...!

“Mihri!”

“I’m sorry, Yildiz...
I knew it... I...!”

“...It was your mother’s gift to you.”

“Your power to shield away flames...
Wasn’t that your mother’s power?”

...This isn’t my power, but...
my mother’s...?
Then, she said “It will all be alright” because...
she was protecting me...?

Mother gave her life to protect me...
Back then, and now...
This whole time...!

...! I’m sorry for not understanding
what you meant...!
Thank you for protecting me...!
But...I wanted you to survive too, Mother...!

The feeling stirring in my chest
became a light
that spread over everything around us.

“It’s not hot anymore.”
The girl’s words made a tear
slide down my cheek.
Escaping the fire with her,
others began to follow us, one after another.

“I won’t let any more lives be lost...!”

Seeing us all shrouded in flames,
the soldiers began to back away
with horrified looks on their faces.

Mother...
From now on,
I’ll use the power you protected me with
to save as many lives as I can...!

The laws of the People of the Sand
are absolute.
Breaking any law is unforgivable.

But that day, I broke a law for the first time.

I found an intruder within our territory,
a poison spider at her feet.
It would be dangerous to leave her there,
so I shouted a warning.

“Leave, now!”

But instead of leaving,
the intruder came closer to me.

Watch out!

Without thinking, I shot an arrow,
taking out the poison spider.
But now this meant...
that I saved the intruder...
I-In times like these,
I should just pretend
I did nothing and leave!

“Wait!”

“My name is Ayse...!
Thank you for saving me...!”

When someone introduces themselves,
you must introduce yourself in return—
that is a law too.
So, I would not be doing a bad thing...

“L-Liberia...”

That was my first meeting
with my secret friend—Ayse.

Ayse is amazing.
She can read. I cannot.
Nobody ever taught me.

“In that case, I’ll teach you.”

Ayse offered to help me learn,
but learning is no good. That is a law.

So, I have to say no.
But, I already broke a law...
Huh...? If a law is broken,
a disaster should happen.
So, why did nothing go wrong...?

“Wanting to know something isn’t a bad thing.
Keeping promises is important,
but letting your curiosity be your guide
matters just as much.”

“Curiosity”...? Another word I do not know.
Just like how I do not know
why every day is sparkly-sparkly
now that I met Ayse.
I wonder what that feeling is called?

I want to know...the name of this feeling.
The reason I look forward to every morning
after meeting Ayse.
I want Ayse...to teach me.

“Then, let’s make this our little secret.
That way, you won’t have to worry about
anyone getting mad at you, right?”

A secret...? Then, maybe...

After that, I learned the alphabet from Ayse.
Learning is very fun.
But, me and Ayse are different in every way...

What I like, I want Ayse to like, too...
So, I made her a mud bath.
But, Ayse would not get in...

Still, I did not give up.
I chased her...but Ayse got mad.
She yelled that she was going to leave...

I do not know why she got mad.
But, I did not want this to be goodbye.
I want to be with Ayse more. And, I...

“I want...to know Ayse.”

I want to learn,
because I do not know Ayse yet.
That is not a bad thing.
Just like Ayse taught me.

I slowly stuck my hand out toward Ayse,
and she gently took it.

“I’m sorry, Liberia.”

“I...want to know you, too...
Because...I want to be your friend, Liberia.”

“Friend”... Only Gran Gran
can give permission to make friends.
That is the law. So, breaking it is no good.
But...I...do not want to pretend
I never had these feelings.
Because, I...

“Ayse, my friend... I am happy...!”

Even if breaking the law was not right,
my heart felt lighter—
far lighter than it ever did
when I followed the law.

After that, me and Ayse
became even better friends.
We fought sometimes,
but we always made up right away.

I thought we would be friends forever.
But...breaking the law,
really was no good, after all.

“Kill that outsider!”

Yelling that, the guards circled around Ayse.
Killing intruders is the law.
If I do not do something, Ayse will be...

“Do not kill her!”

I jumped in front of Ayse right away.
Everyone glared at me.

I-I am scared. But...Ayse is my friend!
I will protect her, no matter what!

“Hmph! What a waste...!
And just when I had you
good and fooled, too.”

Huh...? Ayse...?

I turned around,
and Ayse was looking at me with cold eyes.
Why...is she glaring at me...?

“Did you really think the likes of you
could ever become friends
with someone like me?”

Did I...do something wrong?
Something to make Ayse mad...?
Then, I will make it right! So...!

“Liberia!”

Ayse was shouting
as she rushed towards me.
Her eyes burning as if
an enemy was in front of her.
So, she really...

I shut my eyes and braced myself.
Then, a pained cry rang out.

Ay...se...?

I was scared to look,
but when I opened my eyes...

“Ayse!”

I saw the dagger I was holding,
stuck deep in Ayse’s belly.

A-Ah... I...I did this...to Ayse...?

Ayse looked up at me with a weak smile...

“The two of us...
should never have met after all...huh...?”

Why are you...smiling like that?
Looking so pleased?
I stabbed you...so, why?!

I do not understand. Nothing makes sense.
I do not understand, so teach me...Ayse...!

But she did not respond.
Her eyes would not open.

I...killed...Ayse.

“...It was a mistake to meet Ayse.”

A voice I did not know echoed in my head.

Who said that...?
Could it be...one of the Gods of Sand?

Right, Ayse said so, too.
We should not...have met...

Because, if she had not met me...
Ayse would not have died!

Everything was a mistake.
Meeting Ayse, wanting to learn...
spending time together, having fun...
Becoming...friends...

Before I realized,
a storm of sand had begun
whipping around me.
It withered the plants,
and returned them to the land.

Life once withered can never be returned.
If only...my heart could shrivel, too...

Shrivel and crumble away...
along with my memories with Ayse.
If everything withers away into nothing,
maybe then...
I could pretend we never met...?

If I could just erase
all those mistaken memories...

“Goodbye...Ayse...”

The sand,
which withered every form of life it touched,
began to consume the world.

“Liberia!”

Is that Ayse’s voice? But...how...?

Breaking through the storm of sand,
Ayse stretched her hand towards me.
But, I did not take it.
Because, me and Ayse cannot be together...!

The storm of sand grew stronger.
But, Ayse did not give up.

“I’m sorry, Liberia.
But, the truth is...
I was happy to be your friend!
The two of us meeting
wasn’t a mistake!”

It was...!
Because, if we had not met,
Ayse would not have...!

“I don’t want to be separated from you!
Because...I want to stay as your friend.
That’s how I feel. What about you?”

My feelings do not matter.
Because, if I follow how I feel,
I will only make another mistake.
So, I should just follow our laws...

“What matters is what you want!
Try and remember!
How you felt the first day I taught you!”

...I remember. That day, Ayse taught me.
She said following how I feel
is just as important as
following the laws of my tribe.

How I feel...?
There is only one thing I want to do. I...

“I want to be with you...!”

I reached out,
and Ayse squeezed my hand tightly.

“Yeah... I want to be with you, too, Liberia...!”

Ayse’s hands were so warm.
She broadened my horizons
and awakened these feelings within me,
so meeting her
could never be a mistake.
Because...that is what I believe.

“I am happy I met you, Ayse.”

There are still lots of things I do not know.
I am sure that is the same for her...
So, from today,
we can keep teaching each other new things.
That is something
only the two of us together can do.

Something only us friends can do—

“Find us if you can~!”

Nina and I called that out together,
as we hid in some bushes.
This feels kinda familiar somehow...
What was it again?

Oh, right! It’s like the time we played
hide-and-seek at the lake!
Moddey was there too,
and we all had so much fun!

“’Tis useless trying to hide from me,
you little whelps!”

Ack! She found us already!
Tama sure is good at finding us,
it’s almost scary.

“Now it’s our turns to be the seekers, right?”
“Heh-heh! You little whelps
believe you can best me?”

Ever since I came to live at Master’s mansion,
every single day’s been filled with fun.

And soon, it’ll be my birthday!
I just know it’s gonna be
an even more fun day than today.
I can’t wait! Ehehe!

Phew! Playing together with Tama and Nina
today sure was fun!

Hm? Is that...Artie and Richesse?

“Richesse, thank you for everything.”
“What’re you talking about, partner?
It’s your birthday,
so we’ve gotta make sure
today’s reeeal flashy!”

So, it’s Artie’s birthday today.
That must be why she looks so happy.

That reminds me... When I was little,
I’m pretty sure Big Sis made me candies
for my birthday once.

It made me so happy, I asked her for more.
So, she promised that she’d make some
for me every year.

Ever since then,
I’d look forward to my birthday
even more than before.
It was so exciting—
hearing the sounds of the pot bubbling,
smelling the sweet scent of melted sugar,
and seeing Big Sis put on her serious face...

Seeing her put all that effort in,
just for me, always made me so happy...
I really loved it...

But, after we were abandoned
on that mountain,
she never made those candies for me again.

Sometimes I wonder...
did she forget her promise?
Will I never be able to have
Big Sis’s handmade candies ever again...?
As it got closer to my birthday,
a sweet smell just like this one
would fill the house...

...Huh? This scent... Could it be...?

Sniff, sniff... It’s coming from over here!
I followed the scent
and scurried into the kitchen.
There, I saw Big Sis standing
in front of a large pot on the stove.

“Big Sis! Is that what I think it is...?”
“I’m making candy.”

“I knew it, I knew it!
Big Sis remembered after all!”

“Of course! I’m going to give you
a special candy this year,
so make sure you look forward to it, okay?”

“Hehe, yaaaay~!♪
I’m so happy I can finally have
Big Sis’s candy again!
Oh, I know, I know!”

“Let me help, too!”

I’d always just sat in the kitchen
and watched before, but this year,
I wanna make candies together!

“Um, I just need to stir this, right?
Ngh...it’s not mixing well...”

I wanted to help out Big Sis
for a change,
but...urgh...
It’s not going at all
how I thought it would...

“If you stir too hard, it’ll spill!
See—stir it slowly and gently, like this.”

Big Sis cupped her hands over mine
and helped me mix.

Wow! The super tough candy’s
mixing so smoothly now!
Big Sis really is amazing!

After we finished stirring,
Big Sis poured the melted candy
into another pot.

“All we need to do now
is add some of our witch power,
and it’ll be done!”

Huh? Witch...power?

Witch power...
Just the mention of it
brought back memories of that night.

That dark night,
when hungry creatures attacked us...
A mysterious power surged out of me,
and I... I hurt Big Sis...!

...I know I can’t stay this way forever.
I wanna be strong, just like Big Sis.

But, I’m scared...
Every day I spend with Big Sis
only makes me love her more.
But at the same time,
I get more scared to use my power...!

What if I lose control
and hurt Big Sis again...or Master...?
What if this time, I actually...k-kill...?

“It’s alright, Cerberus.”

Big Sis wrapped her warm hands
around my trembling fingers.
Ah...Big Sis’s hands.
They’ve never failed to protect me.
Because she’s the kindest big sis
in the whole wide world...

At that moment, a small light
began to glow from our clasped hands.
A gentle, yet powerful light.

“Cerberus, I won’t let go
of your hands no matter what.
So, it’s going to be okay.
You just need a dash of courage!”

Big Sis gripped my hands tighter,
as if she was sharing
her own courage with me.

I’m still scared of losing control.
Whenever I try using my power,
the nightmares from that night
come rushing back. But...

A witch’s power comes from her caring heart.
And now, I feel the kindest magic
in the whole wide world,
born from your heart, Big Sis,
wrapping around me.

“Yeah... If you’re here,
Big Sis, I’ll be okay...!”

The two lights spilling out
from our joined hands blended together,
flooding us in the warmth of its bright glow.
And then—

“Happy birthday, Cerberus!”
“Ehehe~♪ Thanks so much, everyone!”

Today is my birthday.

There were tons of presents,
yummy food, circus acts, games...
Everyone wished me a happy birthday
and it was just so much fun!

But, the part that made me
the happiest was...

“Cerberus... Happy birthday!”

Big Sis!

“Wooow! They’re so sparkly and pretty!”

She handed me the jar of magical candies
we made together.
A one-of-a-kind treasure just for me—
no, for us.

“Sorry I couldn’t make you
any candy until now.
From here on out, though,
I’ll make you candy every year!”
“Then, let’s make them together again!
Next year, and the year after that...
Forever and ever!”

I reached into the jar and out came
two candies stuck together, side by side.
They kinda reminded me of me and Big Sis.

We looked at each other and smiled,
splitting the candy between us.

In my hand was a candy
that was blue like Big Sis.
In hers was one that was green like me.

As for the flavor,
it was the most gentle candy
I’d ever eaten...
with a sweetness just like happiness—

Hehe! Big Sis,
I really do love you...sooo much!

What can be said about
the People of the Sand is this...
If you see them, run.

The rumors say that,
should your paths happen to cross,
your life is forfeit.
That’s why no one dares
step close to their territory.

But, after years of research,
we learned that in their territory
lies the mythic oasis,
which was thought to be only a mirage.
Yes—the key to salvaging
our country’s future.

Someday soon,
this country will dry into a basin of dust,
becoming uninhabitable.
So, it’s our mission as researchers
to find that oasis before it’s too late...

Honestly, going there
is the last thing I want to do...
The mere thought makes me shiver...

But, this is a necessary step
to salvaging our country’s future.
I won’t back down until I find that oasis,
no matter what...!

I journeyed to
the People of the Sand’s territory
with our expedition team,
but got separated on the way there.
And, to top it off...

“Leave, now!”

Ugh...! To think I’d run into a member
of the People of the Sand now of all times...!
But, she is just a kid...

“W-Wait! If you just listen to what I—”

Just as I took a step towards her,
an arrow pierced the sand by my feet.
I-I guess the rumors are true, after all...!
...Oh...?

When I inspected further,
I realized that the arrow had pierced
a poisonous variety of desert spider.
Did she just...save me...?

Lifting my head,
I saw the girl preparing to flee...

“Wait!”

As she turned back, our eyes met.
They were doe-like, beautiful eyes—
