■Types​
Characters are classified into 3 types—Warriors, Snipers, and Sorcerers.​

Warriors can equip swords, with their basic attacks and skills comprising of physical attacks.​
The unique type stat that infuences their ATK is STR.​

Snipers can equip pistols, with their basic attacks and skills comprising of physical attacks.​
The unique type stat that infuences their ATK is DEX.​

Sorcerers can equip tomes, with their basic attacks and skills comprising of magical attacks.​
The unique type stat that infuences their ATK is MAG.​

■Souls​
Characters will have 1 of 6 Souls—Azure, Crimson, Emerald, Amber, Radiance, and Chaos.​
Souls are strong or weak against each other, as shown in the pattern below.​

Azure > Crimson > Emerald > Amber > Azure​

Radiance and Chaos are both strong and weak against each other.​

■Active Skills​
An Active Skill is a skill that activates on a character's action phase.​
Active Skills automatically activate starting from the one
that is first available to activate.​
After an Active Skill activates, it will enter its skill cooldown time.​
While the Active Skill is cooling down,
its skill cooldown time will decrease by 1
at the end of each turn's action phase.
When the skill cooldown time's count reaches 0,
the skill will be able to reactivate.​
If all of a character's Active Skills have entered their skill cooldown times,​
that character will perform basic attacks instead.​

■Passive Skills​
A Passive Skill is a skill that automatically activates at a specific time.​
Each Passive Skill has a different activation time, such as the start of a turn,​
when a character is attacked, when a character is defeated, etc.​
If the timing of a Passive Skill's activation is not written in its description,​
that means it activates at the start of the battle.
If a character's Passive Skill meets its activation requirement at the same time​
as that of another character, the activation order of those Passive Skills​
will be determined by the order of the characters' action phases.​
Passive Skills that activate when a character deals an attack,
or is dealt an attack,​ do not activate when the attack is evaded.
A Passive Skill generally does not activate via an effect
of a different Passive Skill.
Effects from basic attacks that are enhanced
via the Strengthened Basic Attack buff​ can also fulfill
requirements for a Passive Skill's activation.
However, the effects of damage cutting and surviving with 1 HP
can activate via the effects of different Passive Skills.

■Turns
The word "turn" used in skill descriptions
can refer to either of the following.

・The TURN count written at the top of the battle screen
・The turn count of a character's action phases

■The TURN Count Written at the Top of the Battle Screen
This refers to the turn count referenced in conditions such as
"the Xth turn," "in X turns," or "from the Xth turn."
It is also referenced in the following.

At the start of a/each turn:
Refers to the TURN count displayed at the top of the battle screen,
which changes after all characters' action phases have ended.

At the end of a/each turn:
Refers to the TURN count displayed at the top of the battle screen,
after all characters' action phases have ended,
up until the next turn count is displayed.

During a turn/This turn:
Refers to the TURN count displayed at the top of the battle screen,
up until the next turn count is displayed.

Over the past X turns:
Refers to all turns up to the specified number of turns prior to
the current turn, based on the current turn count.

■The Turn Count of a Character's Action Phases
This refers to the turn count referenced in conditions
such as the duration of buffs or debuffs, like in "for X turns."

For X turns:
Refers to the number of action phases until
the specified buff or debuff the specified character
is enhanced or afflicted with ends.
If a buff or debuff is applied to a character,
such as when that character's active skill grants them a buff,
from the time that character starts their action phase
until that action phase ends,
that buff or debuff's effect will immediately be applied,
but the effect turn count for that buff or debuff will start
after the end of their action phase the following turn.

■Target Selection​
Each skill selects its target(s) in 1 of 4 ways:​
"Random," "Stat Hierarchy," "Directly in Front," and "Adjacent."​

■Random
Targets are selected at random.​
Placement in the party formation also affects the selection,​
as there is a higher probability a character will target the enemy
directly in front of them,​ and a lower probability to target
an enemy that is further away from that position.​
If a skill prioritizes selecting a target that fulfills a certain condition,
such as skills that say, "This attack prioritizes attacking enemies
who are enhanced with [Multi-Barrier]," a target is selected at random
out of the enemies who fulfill that condition.
If there are no targets the skill can prioritize selecting
because no enemies fulfill the condition,
a target will be selected completely at random.​

■Stat Hierarchy​
Targets are selected based on the hierarchy of a specific stat,​
such as "the enemy with the highest ATK" or​
"the 3 enemies with the lowest remaining HP percentages."​
For "the enemy with the highest ATK," the target becomes the enemy​
with the highest ATK among all remaining enemies.​
For "the 3 enemies with the lowest remaining HP percentages,"​
the targets become the 3 enemies with the lowest remaining HP percentages​
among all remaining enemies.
If there are multiple characters that meet the same condition,​
the target will be selected based on their position in the party formation,​
prioritizing the character placed in the higher slot.​
If a single skill deals multiple attacks,
the stat hierarchy​ will be referenced with each individual attack.
When it comes to referenced stats,​
if a skill activates "at the start of the battle" and "at the start of the 1st turn,"
pre-increased/decreased stats will be referenced.
For other skills, each time a target selection based on a stat is made,
the in-battle stat will be referenced.
*For details on pre-increased/decreased stats, in-battle stats, etc.,
please check the "Scopes of Referenced Stats" section.

■Directly in Front
The target selected is the enemy located in the same party formation​ slot
as the character using the skill.​
If the enemy located directly in front of a character has already been defeated,​
the target will be selected from the remaining enemies at random.
If all enemies targeted by a skill
that targets multiple enemies have already been defeated,
including the enemy located directly in front of a character,
the target will be selected​ from the remaining enemies at random.

■Adjacent
The target will be selected from 1 specific character​
and the characters located on either side of them in a party formation.​
If there are no characters located on either side of the specific character,​
1 character in the party will be forcibly selected at random as a target.​

■Selection Priority​
If buffs, debuffs, etc., cause target selection conditions
to overlap with each other,​
the decision of which target will be selected will be made
based on the following conditions (in order of priority).

If a character is afflicted with Confusion​
▼
If a character uses a skill dealt to the enemy directly in front of them​,
and 1 or more enemies adjacent to that target
▼
If a character is enhanced with Stealth​
▼​
If a character uses a skill that selects a target based on stat hierarchy​
▼​
If a character is enhanced with Taunt​
▼​
If a character uses a skill that is dealt to enemies at random,​
or enemies who are selected at random out of the possible targets
prioritized for fulfilling a certain condition

Characters who are enhanced with Invisibility, or are defeated,
cannot be selected as targets.

■Physical Attacks​
The damage from these attacks is calculated based on a target's P. DEF stat.​
If a critical hit is dealt, damage is calculated based on a target's
P. CRIT DMG Cut stat.​

■Magical Attacks​
The damage from these attacks is calculated based on a target's M. DEF stat.​
If a critical hit is dealt, damage is calculated based on a target's
M. CRIT DMG Cut stat.​

■Direct Attacks​
These attacks deal damage directly to a target,
ignoring their DEF, P. DEF, and M. DEF stats.

■Buffs/Debuffs​
Buffs put characters at an advantage during battle.​​
Debuffs put characters at a disadvantage during battle.​​
Placing a buff on a character is called "granting."​​
Placing a debuff on a character is called "inflicting."​​
Having a buff granted on a character is called being "enhanced."​​
Having a debuff inflicted on a character is called being "afflicted."​​
Characters who grant buffs are called "granters."​​
Characters who inflict debuffs are called "inflictors."​​
Characters who have been granted buffs are called "enhanced targets."​​
Characters who have been inflicted with debuffs are called "afflicted targets."​
The decision to inflict a debuff is made based on a character's chance​
to inflict a debuff​ and the target's chance to resist a debuff.​
There are specific skills that dispel buffs/debuffs, copy them onto targets, or steal them.​​
If the number of buffs/debuffs the target has exceeds​​
the number that can be dispelled, copied, or stolen,​​
buffs/debuffs will be selected at random​​
from those the target is currently enhanced or afflicted with.​
​
■A Buff/Debuff's Effect Turn Count​​
If a buff or debuff specifies the number of turns​
its effect will last,​ like in "for X turns,"​
its effects will last only until its effect turn count reaches 0.​
Once a character's action phase is over,​
an effect's turn count will decrease by 1.​​
However, if a buff or debuff is applied to a character,​
such as when that character's active skill grants them a buff,​
from the time that character starts their action phase
until that action phase ends,
that buff or debuff's effect will immediately be applied,
but the effect turn count for that buff or debuff will start
after the end of their action phase the following turn.
Once its effect turn count reaches 0, that buff/debuff will be dispelled.​​
Additionally, certain skills can be used to increase/decrease​
the effect turn count of a buff/debuff.​​
​
■Effect Overlapping​​
Aside from a few exceptions,​
buffs/debuffs that have the same type of effect can overlap with each other.​
​
The following is an example of when effects can overlap.​​
If a target is already enhanced with an effect that increases their ATK,​​
and an ally grants that target a different effect that increases their ATK,​​
both ATK-increasing effects can overlap.​
​
The following is an example of when effects cannot overlap.​​
If Enfeeble, Fainted, Poison, Bleed, Burn, Erosion, and Aggravation​
are each inflicted more than once,​ the effect of each debuff will be overwritten.​​
When an effect is overwritten, only one of that effect will remain on the target.​​
It will carry over the largest values for the effect turn count and effect size.​​
​
Excluding effects that can be stacked,​
if the same buff/debuff becomes overlapped​ on the same character,​
the new buff/debuff will overwrite the old one.​​
​
■Effect Stacking​​
Some buffs/debuffs can be stacked if they have an effect that increases in size​​
each time that buff/debuff is given to a target.​​
The number of times the buff/debuff is given to a target​
is added to the stack count,​ and there is a limit to how many times​
the effect can be stacked.​​
If a stacked buff/debuff is dispelled, its stack count will become 0.​​
​
■Dispelling​​
A target's buff or debuff can be dispelled.​​
The decision to dispel a target's buff will be made​
based on​ a character's chance to inflict a debuff​
and the target's chance to resist a debuff.
The decision to dispel multiple buffs or debuffs,
unless otherwise specified in the effect's description,
will be made separately for each buff/debuff,
based on the character's chance to inflict a debuff
and the target's chance to resist a debuff,
as well as the chance (%) the dispelling will happen.
​
■Turn Increasing/Decreasing​
This refers to the increase or decrease​
of the effect turn count for a specified buff or debuff.​
Decreasing an enemy's buff's effect turn count,
or increasing an enemy's debuff's effect turn count,
are both decided based on​
the character's chance to inflict a debuff​
and the enemy's chance to resist a debuff.​
When the effect turn count of a buff or debuff reaches 0​
due to a skill with an effect that decreases turn counts,​
that buff or debuff will be dispelled.​
​
■Buff Copying​​
This allows a character to grant themselves a buff​
that a target is enhanced with.​​
Devotion, as well as buffs that say "cannot be dispelled" in their description​
cannot be copied.​
The value of the copied buff's effect will not be changed or updated​
from the time it was copied.​
​
■Debuff Copying​​
This allows a character to inflict a debuff they are afflicted with on an enemy.​​
The decision to afflict a copied debuff will be decided based on​​
a character's chance to inflict a debuff​
and the target's chance to resist a debuff.​​
Resonance, as well as debuffs that say​
"cannot be dispelled" in their descriptions, cannot be copied.​
The value of the copied debuff's effect will not be changed​
or updated from the time it was copied.​
As an exception, the amount of continuous damage caused via Burn or Poison,​
as well as the maximum amount of continuous damage,​
is calculated based on the in-battle stats of the character​
the debuff is copied to.​
The amount a stat is decreased by via Enfeeble​
is also calculated based on the in-battle stats of the character​
the debuff is copied to.​
​
■Steal​​
This allows a character to dispel a target's buff and grant it to themselves.​
The decision to dispel a buff and grant it to the character are both made​
at the same time hance (%) written in the skill description.​
In addition to the chance written in the skill description,​
the decision to dispel the target's buff is made based on​
the character's chance to inflict a debuff​
and the target's chance to resist a debuff.​
Devotion, Resonance, and buffs that say "cannot be dispelled"​
in their description cannot be stolen.​
The value of the stolen buff's effect will not be changed or updated​
from the time it was stolen.​
As an exception, the amount of continuous damage caused via Burn or Poison,​
as well as those debuffs' maximum amount of continuous damage,​
and stat decreases caused via Enfeeble,​
are calculated based on the in-battle stats of the character​
the stolen effect is applied to.​
​
■Buffs/Debuffs that Cannot be Dispelled​​
Buffs/debuffs that "cannot be dispelled," as written in their descriptions,​​
have the following traits.​​
They do not count as buffs/debuffs that are "enhancing" or "afflicting" a target.​​
Buffs/debuffs such as "Increased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,"​
count towards requirements that are referenced for specific actions.​
Their effects cannot be subject to dispelling,​
effect turn increasing/decreasing, copying, or stealing.​
They are not affected by a character's chance to inflict a debuff,​
a target's chance to resist a debuff, Buff Immunity, or Debuff Immunity.​​
With the exception of some effects, these buffs/debuffs will not be displayed​​
as icons during battle.​
Buffs/debuffs that cannot be dispelled are included​
as activation requirements for skills that activate​
when buffs or debuffs are granted or inflicted via active skills.​

■Increased Stat​
This buff increases a specified stat.​
The pre-increased/decreased stat is referenced
to calculate the amount the buff increases it by.

■Increased Damage Dealing​
This buff increases the damage a character deals when they attack.​

■Decreased Damage Taken​
This buff decreases the damage a character takes when they are attacked.​

■Increased Incoming Healing Potency
This buff increases the amount of HP restored to a character
when they take an HP-restoring effect.
This affects skills that restore HP, Regeneration, and HP Drain.

■Invulnerable​
This buff nullifies damage a character takes.​

■Multi-Barrier​
This buff provides a multi-layered barrier.
When a character takes damage,​
1 barrier layer is depleted to nullify that damage.​
If Multi-Barrier is overlapped with Invulnerable,
the barrier layer will not be depleted.​
If Multi-Barrier is overlapped with Shield,
Multi-Barrier will be used first.
If multiple kinds of Multi-Barrier are overlapping with each other,
they will be used based on the following order of priority.

Multi-Barriers with fewer effect turns left
▼
Multi-Barriers with larger amounts of damage
required for activation
▼
Multi-Barriers with fewer layers left

■Shield​
This buff provides a shield that nullifies a designated amount of damage.​
When a character takes damage that exceeds the amount that can be nullified,​
the shield will be depleted, and the remaining damage will be dealt
to the character's HP.​
If Shield is overlapped with Invulnerable, Shield will not be depleted.​
If Shield is overlapped with Multi-Barrier, Multi-Barrier will be used first.​

■Force Field
This buff reduces a designated amount of damage
from attacks, Resonance, Devotion, and counterattack damage.
Damage from Poison and other debuffs that deal continuous damage
cannot be reduced.
The effects of Increased/Decreased Damage Taken
and Increased/Decreased Damage Dealing
are calculated before damage is reduced via Force Field.
The effects of Shield, Resonance, and Devotion are calculated
after damage is reduced via Force Field.​
When the effect of multiple Force Fields activates,
or when the effects of Force Field
and cutting activate at the same time,
the only effect that will be applied will be the one that results
in the least amount of damage
being ultimately dealt to the character.

■Debuff Immunity​
This buff prevents debuffs from being inflicted on a character.​
This does not nullify any debuffs a character is already afflicted with.​

■Unhindered​
This buff prevents action hindering debuffs from being inflicted on a character.​
There are 4 action hindering debuffs—Fainted, Sleep, Confusion, and Silence.​
This does not nullify any action hindering debuffs a character
is already afflicted with.​

■Silence Immunity​
This buff prevents Silence from being inflicted on a character.​
This does not nullify any Silence debuffs
a character is already afflicted with.​

■Taunt​
This buff guarantees a character is the target of enemy attacks and skills
dealt to 1 or more random targets.​
This does not make that character the target if the enemy attack or skill
is not dealt to random targets.​

■Stealth​
This buff prevents a character from being a target
of enemy attacks and skills dealt to 1 target.​
However, that character can be the target of attacks and skills
that are dealt to the target directly in front of the attacker.​
If all allies who are alive are enhanced with either Stealth or Invisibility,
the effect of Stealth will be nullified.

■Invisibility​
This buff prevents a character from being a target of attacks and skills
of enemies and allies.​
If all allies who are alive are enhanced with Invisibility,
the effect of Invisibility will be nullified.

■Counter-Fainted
This buff gives a character a chance to inflict Fainted
on their attacker when attacked.

■Regeneration​
This buff restores a specified amount of HP to a character each turn​
at the start of that character's action phase.​

■Immortality​
This buff guarantees a character survives with 1 HP remaining​
if they take damage that would reduce their HP to 0.​
This includes damage taken from attacks, Resonance, and Devotion.
This also includes damage from Poison and other debuffs
that deal continuous damage, as well as counterattack damage.

■Counter Shift​
When attacked by an enemy, this buff allows a character to deal​
a designated amount of counterattack damage
to a specific enemy instead of dealing a regular counterattack.​
The amount of damage is not affected by the Counter stat
(even if [Increased Counter] or
[Decreased Counter] are applied to it).
Additionally, the amount of damage taken by a character
has no effect on this buff's counterattack damage.
Counter Shift is guaranteed to hit, but is not factored in
when counting the number of attacks that are dealt to an enemy.
Counter Shift does not activate when a character
takes damage from Poison
and other debuffs that deal continuous damage,
Resonance, Devotion, or Passive Skills.
Counter Shift activates only when an attack hits.
It does not activate when an attack is evaded.

■Devotion
This buff allows an enhanced target to substitutively take
a designated amount of damage
from the damage an attack would deal to another ally.
If the amount of damage taken by an ally exceeds their remaining HP,​
the amount of damage exceeding that ally's remaining HP will also be included​
in the damage dealt to the enhanced target.
If damage would be taken via Devotion and Resonance at the same time,
the damage will be totaled together and count as 1 instance of taking damage.

■Buff Cover
When 1 of the enhanced target's buffs would be dispelled or stolen by an enemy's skill,​
this buff will be dispelled or stolen with the highest priority out of all buffs
the target is enhanced with.​
If the target is enhanced with multiple Buff Covers,
1 will be dispelled or stolen at random.​
For skills that lower a buff's turn count or stack count,​
Buff Cover will not be prioritized for dispelling.

■Hasten​
This buff speeds up the decrease of a character's​
Active Skills' skill cooldown time​
at the end of each turn's action phase,​
effectively hastening the next time that character's Active Skills activate.​
If Hasten is overlapped with Delay,
the final amount that the skill cooldown time decreases by will be decided
by how much​ the effects of Delay offset the effects of Hasten.

■Character-Specific Buffs
These are buffs granted by the skills of specific characters.
The effects of the buffs vary depending on the character-specific buff.

■Decreased Stat​
This debuff decreases a specified stat.​
The pre-increased/decreased stat is referenced
to calculate the amount the debuff decreases it by.​

■Enfeeble
This debuff decreases a character's ATK.
Unlike normal Decreased Stat debuffs,
the amount a target's stat is decreased by via Enfeeble
is calculated based on their in-battle stat.

■Decreased Damage Dealing​
This debuff decreases the damage a character deals when they attack.​

■Increased Damage Taken​
This debuff increases the damage a character takes when they are attacked.​

■Decreased Incoming Healing Potency​
This buff decreases the amount of HP restored to a character​
when they take an HP-restoring effect.​
This affects skills that restore HP, Regeneration, and HP Drain.​

■Delay
This debuff stalls the decrease of a character's​
Active Skills' skill cooldown time​
at the end of each turn's action phase,​
effectively delaying the next time that character's Active Skills activate.​
The final amount that a skill cooldown time decreases by​
will never be less than 0.​
If Delay is overlapped with Hasten,
the final amount​ that the skill cooldown time decreases by will be decided
by how much​ the effects of Delay offset the effects of Hasten.

■Action Hindering Debuffs
The debuffs that fall under this category are
Silence, Fanted, Sleep, and Confusion.

・Silence
This debuff makes a character unable to activate Active Skills.
The afflicted character can only deal basic attacks.

・Fainted
This debuff makes a character unable to deal basic attacks
or activate Active Skills, ending that character's action phase.

・Sleep
This debuff makes a character unable to deal basic attacks
or activate Active Skills, ending that character's action phase.
This is dispelled after the specified number of turns,
or by other specific conditions.

・Confusion
This debuff makes a character select either allies other than themselves or enemies at random
as attack targets.
Even skills that specify its targets to be the enemy with the highest ATK, etc.,
will be dealt to enemies or allies at random.
Skills that make allies targets, as well as skills that affect allies and enemies
at the same time, are not affected by Confusion.
When characters are afflicted with Confusion,
they will not be affected by Taunt or Stealth.

■Debuffs that Deal Continuous Damage
The debuffs that fall under this category are Poison, Burn, Bleed, and Erosion.

・Poison
Each turn, at the start of the action phase,
this debuff makes the afflicted character take continuous damage
based on a percentage of their current HP.
The damage will not exceed the afflicted character's ATK stat value.

・Burn
Each turn, at the start of the action phase,
this debuff makes the afflicted character take continuous damage
based on a percentage of their current HP.
The damage will not exceed the afflicted character's ATK stat value.

・Bleed
Each turn, at the start of the action phase,
this debuff makes the afflicted character take continuous damage
based on a percentage of the inflictor's ATK.

・Erosion
Each turn, at the start of the action phase,
this debuff makes the afflicted character take continuous damage
based on a percentage of the total damage dealt by the skill
that inflicted Erosion.
The total damage dealt will be calculated based on its value
before it is reduced by cutting, Multi-Barrier, and Shield.

■Aggravation
This debuff increases the continuous damage a character takes.
If the continuous damage from Poison/Burn is increased via Aggravation,
that continuous damage will not exceed the ATK stat value
of the character who is afflicted with Poison/Burn.

■Blight​
This debuff prevents a character from having their HP restored.​
This affects skills that restore HP, Regeneration, and HP Drain.​

■Buff Immunity​
This debuff prevents buffs from being granted to a character.​
This does not nullify any buffs a character is already enhanced with.​
While a character is afflicted with Buff Immunity,
if a buff updates the value of a stat, etc.,​
when specific conditions are met, those increases will not be applied.​
Buff Immunity does not affect buffs that cannot be dispelled.​

■Bind​
This debuff makes a character unable to evade enemy attacks.​

■Resonance​
This debuff is inflicted on two characters,​​
and when one afflicted target takes damage from an attack,​
a designated amount of that damage is dealt to the other afflicted target.​
If the amount of damage taken by one target exceeds their remaining HP,​
the amount of damage exceeding that target's remaining HP will also be​
included in the damage dealt to the other afflicted target.
​If damage would be taken via Devotion and Resonance at the same time,
the damage will be totaled together and count as 1 instance of taking damage.

■Character-Specific Debuffs
These are buffs afflicted by the skills of specific characters.
The effects of the debuffs vary depending on the character-specific debuff.

■If/When a Character is Attacked​
This condition causes certain skills to activate upon being fulfilled.
It will only be fulfilled if the character is successfully hit by an attack.
It will not fulfilled if the attack is evaded,
or if counterattack damage is dealt to the character.
If the character is hit by an attack, but buffs such as Shield or Multi-Barrier
reduce the damage to 0, this condition will still be fulfilled.

■HP Restoration​
This effect restores a character's HP by a designated amount.​

■Defeated​
When a character's HP drops to 0, they are defeated.​
Defeated characters cannot perform any actions.​
When a character is defeated, all their buffs/debuffs are dispelled.​
Additionally, the value of a character's skill cooldown time
at the moment right before​ they were defeated
will remain unchanged.

■Damage Dealt
​This is damage dealt to a target by an attack.
​Any amount of damage that exceeds a target's remaining HP
is also counted towards the amount of damage dealt.
This corresponds to damage before damage reductions are factored in
via ​Shield, Multi-Barrier, Invulnerable, cutting,
surviving with 1 HP, and Immortality.
Skills that reference the damage dealt to a target
are calculated before damage reductions are factored in
via the buffs and effects above.

*Example: Stella's Active Skill "Unleash the Evil Eye," Lv 1
"Deals 1 physical attack equal to 800% of her ATK
to the enemy with the highest ATK,
and restores HP equal to 25% of this skill's total damage to the ally
with ​the lowest remaining HP percentage."
​In the skill description above, "25% of this skill's total damage"
is the part of this skill ​that references the damage dealt to a target.

■Damage Taken
This is damage taken by a character from an attack.
Any amount of damage that exceeds a character's remaining HP
is not counted towards the amount of damage taken.
This corresponds to damage after damage reductions are factored in via
Shield, Multi-Barrier, Invulnerable, cutting,
surviving with 1 HP, and Immortality.
Skills that reference the damage taken by a character
are calculated after damage reductions are factored in
via the buffs and effects above.

*Example: Fia's Active Skill "Grim Retribution," Lv 1
"Deals 1 direct attack equal to 10% of the total damage taken by her
​over the past 20 turns to 2 random enemies."
In the skill description above, "10% of the total damage taken by her"
is the part of this skill ​that references the damage taken by a character.

■Increased/Decreased Skill Cooldown Time​
This effect increases or decreases the number of turns
of a target's skill cooldown time.​

■Revive​
When a character takes damage that makes them defeated,​
this effect restores that character's HP
and makes them able to battle again.​
Characters who have taken damage from attacks,
Resonance, and Devotion can be revived.
Characters who have taken damage from Poison
and other debuffs that deal continuous damage,​
as well as counterattack damage, can also be revived.​

■Guaranteed to Hit​
These attacks are guaranteed to hit their target.​
This effect is not affected by a character's Chance to Hit
and Chance to Evade.​

■Guaranteed to Deal a Critical Hit​
These attacks, when they successfully hit their target,​
are guaranteed to deal a critical hit.​
This effect is not affected by a character's Chance to Deal a Critical Hit
and Chance to Resist a Critical Hit.

■Ignore Chance to Inflict a Debuff/Chance to Resist a Debuff​
This effect does not calculate either the inflictor's chance to inflict a debuff​
or the target's chance to resist a debuff when inflicting a debuff,​
with only the chance to inflict a debuff set by the skill being the deciding factor.​
However, if the target is enhanced with [Debuff Immunity],​
even if the skill's chance to inflict a debuff is 100%,​
that debuff will not be inflicted.​

■Ignore Multi-Barrier
This effect deals damage with attacks
without being affected by the target's Multi-Barrier.
The ignored barrier layer will not be depleted.

■Cut​
This effect reduces a specific percentage of damage taken by attacks,
Resonance, and Devotion.
This also reduces a specific percentage of counterattack damage.
Damage from Poison and other debuffs that deal continuous damage
cannot be reduced.
The effects of Increased/Decreased Damage Taken
and Increased/Decreased Damage Dealing
are calculated before damage is reduced via cutting.
The effects of Invulnerable, Multi-Barrier, Shield, Resonance,
and Devotion are calculated after damage is reduced via cutting.
However, in the case of counterattack damage,
the effects of Invulnerable, Multi-Barrier, and Shield
are calculated before damage is reduced via cutting.
When the effects of Force Field and cutting activate at the same time,
the only effect that will be applied will be the one that results
in the least amount of damage being ultimately dealt to the character.

■Survive with 1 HP​
This effect guarantees a character survives with 1 HP remaining​
if they take damage that would reduce their HP to 0.​
This includes damage taken from attacks, Resonance, and Devotion.
This also includes damage from Poison
and other debuffs that deal continuous damage,
as well as counterattack damage.
This effect cannot be dispelled, copied, or stolen.​

■Absorb​
This effect allows a character to inflict
a specific decreased stat debuff on an enemy,​
and grant themselves a buff that increases their corresponding stat
by the decreased amount.​
If the character fails to inflict the debuff, they will not be granted the buff.​

■Strengthened Basic Attack​
This effect strengthens a character's basic attack.​
The way a character's basic attack is strengthened
varies depending on the skill.​
Strengthened Basic Attack cannot be dispelled, copied, stolen,
or have its turn count increased or decreased.
Strengthened Basic Attack buffs cannot be overlapped,​
and if more than one of these buffs are granted to a character,​
the buff that the character will remain enhanced with​
will be based on the following order of priority.​

A Strengthened Basic Attack buff
granted by the character to themselves​
▼​
The most recently granted Strengthened Basic Attack buff​

■Dealing Damage to Self​
This effect decreases a character's HP.​
This is not affected by DEF, P. DEF, M. DEF,
Increased/Decreased Damage Dealing,
Increased/Decreased Damage Taken, Cut,
Invulnerable, Shield, Multi-Barrier, Immortality, or Survive with 1 HP.​

■Counterattack​
When attacked by an enemy, this effect allows a character
to deal counterattack damage back to that enemy.​
The counterattack damage dealt to the enemy depends
on the damage taken from them and the character's Counter stat.​
Damage taken that exceeds the character's remaining HP​
will not be calculated towards the counterattack damage dealt.​​
A counterattack is guaranteed to hit, but is not factored in
when counting the number of attacks that are dealt to an enemy.
A counterattack does not activate when a character takes damage
from Poison​ and other debuffs that deal continuous damage,
Resonance, Devotion, or Passive Skills.​
A counterattack activates only when an attack hits.
It does not activate when an attack is evaded.​
*The "counterattack" effect described here is separate
from a character's "Counter" stat.

■Counterattack Damage
This is damage dealt to an enemy via a counterattack or by Counter Shift.
​Counterattack damage is affected by Cut, Shield, Multi-Barrier,
Invulnerable, and Immortality.
​Additionally, counterattack damage is not affected by
​Increased/Decreased Damage Dealing,
Increased/Decreased Damage Taken, DEF, P. DEF, or M. DEF.

■HP Drain​
When attacking an enemy, this effect restores a character's HP​
depending on the amount of damage they deal and their HP Drain stat.​
The amount of HP restored is calculated based on how much damage
is dealt​ after the following effects are factored in:​
Cut, Shield, Multi-Barrier, Invulnerable, and Immortality.​
Damage that exceeds the enemy's remaining HP​
will not be calculated towards the amount of HP restored.​
HP Drain does not activate when a character takes damage
from Poison​ and other debuffs that deal continuous damage,
Resonance, Devotion, or Passive Skills.​
HP Drain activates only when an attack hits.
It does not activate when an attack is evaded.

■Increased Chance
The increases caused by Increased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,
Increased Chance to Resist a Critical Hit, Increased Chance to Hit,
Increased Chance to Evade, Increased Chance to Inflict a Debuff,
and Increased Chance to Resist a Debuff
add to each activation decision's likelihood of a success,
which is determined based on the stats of a character and target.
Additionally, the infliction of a debuff
is calculated based on the skill's chance to inflict the debuff.

・For Chance to Deal a Critical Hit
When the likelihood of success of the decision for a character to deal
a critical hit is 60% due to their CRIT and a target's CRIT RES,
and the character is enhanced with a
30% Increased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,
their attack's final chance to deal a critical hit
will be calculated as follows.
▶60%+30%=90%​
If the target is enhanced with a
30% Increased Chance to Resist a Critical Hit,
the character's attack's chance to deal a critical hit
will be calculated as follows.
▶60%-30%=30%

・For Chance to Evade
When the likelihood of success of the decision for a character's attack to hit
is 50%, and the character is enhanced with a 30% Increased Chance to Hit,
the character's attack's chance to hit the target
will be calculated as follows.
▶50%+30%=80%
If the target is enhanced with a
30% Increased Chance to Evade,
the character's attack's chance to hit the target
will be calculated as follows.
▶50%-30%=20%

・For Chance to Inflict a Debuff
When a skill's chance to inflict a debuff is 50%,
the debuff's likelihood of success is 10%
due to the character's Debuff ACC and a target's Debuff RES,
and the character is enhanced with a 20% Chance to Inflict a Debuff,
their final chance to inflict a debuff will be calculated as follows.
▶50%×(100%+10%+20%)=65%
If the target is enhanced with a
20% Increased Chance to Resist a Debuff,
the character's chance to inflict a debuff will be calculated as follows.
▶50%×(100%+10%-20%)=45%

■Decreased Chance
The decreases caused by Decreased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,
Decreased Chance to Resist a Critical Hit, Decreased Chance to Hit,
Decreased Chance to Evade, Decreased Chance to Inflict a Debuff,
and Decreased Chance to Resist a Debuff
subtracts from each activation decision's likelihood of a success,
which is determined based on the stats of a character and target.
Additionally, the infliction of a debuff
is calculated based on the skill's chance to inflict the debuff.

・For Chance to Deal a Critical Hit
When the likelihood of success of the decision for a character to deal
a critical hit is 30% due to the character's CRIT and a target's CRIT RES,
and the character is afflicted with a
40% Decreased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,
their attack's final chance to deal a critical hit
will be calculated as follows.
▶60%-30%=30%
If the target is afflicted with a
30% Decreased Chance to Deal a Critical Hit,
the character's attack's chance to deal a critical hit
will be calculated as follows.
▶60%+30%=90%

・For Chance to Hit​
When the likelihood of success of the decision for a character's attack to hit
is 50%,
and the character is afflicted with a 30% Decreased Chance to Evade,
the character's attack's chance to hit the target​
will be calculated as follows.
▶50%-30%=20%
If the target is afflicted with a
30% Decreased Chance to Evade,
the character's attack's final chance to hit the target
will be calculated as follows.
▶50%+30%=80%

・For Chance to Inflict a Debuff
If a skill's chance to inflict a debuff is 50%,
the debuff's likelihood of success is 10%
due to the character's Debuff ACC and a target's Debuff RES,
and the character is afflicted with a 20% Decreased Chance to Inflict a Debuff,
their final chance to inflict a debuff will be calculated as follows.
▶50%×(100%+10%-20%)=45%
If the target is affliced with a 20% Decreased Chance to Inflict a Debuff,
the character's chance to inflict a debuff will be calculated as follows.
▶50%×(100%+10%+20%)=65%

■Scopes of Referenced Stats
For any effect that references a stat,
the stat that is referenced will fall under 1 of the following 3 categories:
"Character Growth Stats," "Pre-Increased/Decreased Stats,"
and "In-Battle Stats."

■Character Growth Stats
This corresponds to a character's stats that are displayed on their Stats screen,
and their respective values comes from totaling various components together.
These stats are used as the basis for pre-increased/decreased stats,
and are not directly referenced during battle.
A character growth stat includes a character's Potential,
their gear's Base Effect, Bonus Effect, Aug. Effect, and Gear Set Effect,
their unique weapon's Unique Passive Effect,
runes, arcana, and Player Rank Bonuses.

■Pre-Increased/Decreased Stats
This corresponds to a character's stats in their initial states,
before any stat-increasing/decreasing buffs, debuffs, etc.,
are applied to them during battle.
These stats are used as the basis for in-battle stats,
and are also referenced if directly specified during battle.
In addition to the related character growth stat,
a pre-increased/decreased stat includes Soul Bonuses
and the effects gained from the Witch's Gift.

■In-Battle Stats​
This corresponds to a character's stats in their current states,
after all stat increases/decreases have been applied to them during battle.
In addition to the related pre-increased/decreased stat,
an in-battle stat includes all buffs and debuffs
(including blessings, Guild Battle Buffs, and Guild Battle Debuffs).

An in-battle stat also includes buffs and debuffs from Passive Skills
that activate at the start of the battle.
Skills that activate at the start of a battle
are prioritized over skills that activate​ at the start of the 1st turn.

■Action Phases​
On a character's action phase, an Active Skill or basic attack will activate.​
Each character can perform an action phase 1 time each turn.​
A character's action phase will end either after an Active Skill activates​
or after the character performs a basic attack.​
If a character cannot perform any actions due to being afflicted with effects​
from action hindering debuffs, such as Fainted or Sleep,​
that state will be treated as the end of the action phase.​
If an Active Skill reactivates, it does not count as a separate action phase.​
Activations of Passive Skills and counterattacks
can occur outside of action phases.​

If a character's skill description states that the skill or one of its effects
activates "at the start of the action phase,"
that skill or effect will activate at the start of that character's action phase.

■Action Order​
The action order for characters during battle is determined​
by each character's SPD stat values at the start of each turn.​
Thus, the higher a character's SPD stat values are,
the more likely they are to act earlier.
If a character's SPD stat value changes during a turn,
it will not affect their action order​ for that turn.
Instead, the change will affect the action order​
at the start of the following turn.

■Gear​
Equipping gear onto characters will boost their stats.​
If a piece of gear's Gear Lv is higher than a character's Character Lv,​
then it cannot be equipped by that character.​

■Base Effect and Bonus Effect​
Each piece of gear has a Base Effect and a Bonus Effect.​
A different stat will be boosted by the Base Effect based on the body part the piece of gear is for.​
The higher a piece of gear's rarity is, the more stats the Bonus Effect will boost.​
The Bonus Effect's total value will be allocated randomly to each stat
when the piece of gear is equipped.​

■Augment Effect​
Augmenting a piece of gear to give it a Holy Lv and a Dark Lv will activate its Aug. Effect.​
Different stats will be boosted by the Holy Lv and Dark Lv based on the body part
the piece of gear is for.​
Augmenting can raise the Holy Lv and Dark Lv, which will in turn raise the stat boost.​

■Gear Set Effect​
Effects will activate on gear from sets based on the number of gear equipped​
that have the same Gear Set Effect.​
Gear from sets come in 5 rarities—R, SR, SSR, UR, and LR.​
To equip gear with a rarity of LR, the character must have a rarity of LR+5 or above.
You can obtain them by obtaining parts from Gear Invoke, etc.,
and synthesizing them in your Item Box.​

■Unique Weapon​
Equipping a unique weapon on its designated character will activate​
its Unique Skill Effect and Unique Passive Effect.​
Unique weapons come in 3 rarities—SSR, UR, and LR.​
To equip gear with a rarity of LR, the character must have a rarity of LR+5 or above.
Unique weapons also have Gear Set Effects,​
so equipping them alongside other gear from the same set will activate the Gear Set Effect.​

■Upgrading Gear​
By upgrading, you can raise a piece of gear's Upgrade Lv.​​
Raising the Upgrade Lv will boost the piece of gear's Base Effect.​​
A piece of gear's max Upgrade Lv is the same value as its Gear Lv.​​
If you lose a piece of gear via smelting or augmenting,
items used for upgrading will all be returned.​

■Reforging Gear​
Reforging a piece of gear can reallocate its Bonus Effect stat values at random.​
This will not change the Bonus Effect's boosted stats or total value.​
The equipping character's unique type stat is displayed in green.​
Making the unique type stat higher will exhibit the piece of gear's strength even more.​

■Lock Feature​
When you reach a certain VIP Lv, the lock feature will be unlocked.​
By locking a Bonus Effect stat, its value will not change,​
and only the remaining Bonus Effect stat values will be reallocated.​
When you use the lock feature, Diamonds will be spent to reforge.​

This will not change the Bonus Effect's boosted stats or total value.​

■Bulk Reforge​
By using Bulk Reforge, you can reforge a piece of gear 20 times at once​
by selecting 1 reforge result to apply to that piece of gear.​
Bulk Reforge uses a number of items equivalent to 20 reforges.​
Items will be used upon tapping the Reforge button,​
and will not be returned even if you have discarded your reforge results.​

You cannot use the lock feature with Bulk Reforge.​
If you close the app before selecting a reforge result to use,​
the Bonus Effect stat values for that piece of gear​
will return to their state prior to opening the Bulk Reforge selection screen.​

■Bulk Reforge​

and select 1 of those reforge results to apply to that piece of gear.​
Bulk Reforge uses a number of items equal to what is needed to perform 20 reforges.​
Items will be used upon tapping the Reforge button,​
and will not be returned even if you have discarded your reforge results.​

You cannot use the lock feature with Bulk Reforge.​

the Bonus Effect stat values for that piece of gear​
will return to their values prior to when Bulk Reforge was performed.​

■Augmenting Gear​
By augmenting, you can raise a piece of gear's Holy Lv and Dark Lv.​

Gear with a Holy Lv or a Dark Lv can be consumed to augment a piece of gear.​
Dark Perfume can also be used.​

Gear with mounted runes cannot be selected as materials to be consumed.​

■Holy Auto-Select/Dark Auto-Select
By using Holy Auto-Select, you will automatically select materials that can raise
a piece of gear's Holy Lv until you have 7 materials chosen.
Using Dark Auto-Select will do the same with materials that can raise
a piece of gear's Dark Lv.

A piece of gear with both a Holy Lv and Dark Lv will not be automatically selected.

■Set Holy Lv/Set Dark Lv
By using Set Holy Lv, you will automatically select all the materials
required for upgrading a piece of gear to the Holy Lv you set.
Using Set Dark Lv will do the same with all the materials
required for upgrading a piece of gear to the Dark Lv you set.

A piece of gear with a Holy Lv or Dark Lv of 2 or higher will not be selected.
A piece of gear with both a Holy Lv and Dark Lv will not be automatically selected.

■The Number of Materials That Can be Selected at Once
With Holy Auto-Select/Dark Auto-Select,
there is a limit of 7 materials that can be selected at once.
With Set Holy Lv/Set Dark Lv, as well as the manual selection of materials,
there is no limit to the number of items that can be selected at once.

■Enhancing Gear​
Unique weapons and gear with Gear Set Effects can be enhanced.​​
​
Enhancing a piece of gear will raise its Gear Lv, boost its Base Effect/Bonus Effect values,​​
and make the Gear Set Effect even stronger.​​
​
After Gear Lv 240, no more boosts will be applied.​​
Additionally, a piece of gear cannot be enhanced to a Gear Lv exceeding the equipping character's Lv.​

■Awakening Gear​
When a character's rarity becomes LR+5, and they are equipping a unique weapon​
or gear from sets with a UR-rarity that have reached a certain Gear Lv,​
awakening will become available to use.​

Awakening a piece of gear will raise its rarity.​
Raising rarity will boost its Base Effect/Bonus Effect values, make the Gear Set Effect even stronger.​

​■Reset Enhanced Gear​
The Reset Enhanced Gear feature will be unlocked upon both reaching a Party Lv of 360,​
and after obtaining 2 or more types of unique weapons at a rarity of UR or higher.​
The Reset Enhanced Gear feature can be performed on unique weapons at Lv 310 or higher.​
By performing Reset Enhanced Gear on a unique weapon, its Gear Lv will be returned to Lv 300,​
and the items that were used to enhance it will also be returned as materials.​
Any unique weapon parts used to enhance the unique weapon will be returned as Magic Crystals​
in the amount needed to exchange for an equivalent amount of unique weapon parts​
in the Magic Crystal Shop.​
If the unique weapon that is reset has an Upgrade Lv of 301 or higher,​
its Upgrade Lv will also be returned to Lv 300,​
and the items used to upgrade it will also be returned as upgrade materials.​
Unique weapons set to base slots in the Weapon Sync cannot be reset.​

The Reset Enhanced Gear feature can be used 1 time per month.​
The uses for the Reset Enhanced Gear feature will be reset​
on the 1st of each month at 4:00 (Server Time).​

■Gear Transfer​
Doing a gear transfer allows you to transfer a piece of gear's upgraded state to another.​
If the inheritor has already been upgraded, the stronger upgrade values​
between the transferor and the inheritor will be applied to the inheritor,​
and the weaker upgrade values will be applied to the transferor. ​

[Example]
Transferor: Upgrade Lv 3, Holy Lv 2, Dark Lv 5​
Inheritor: Upgrade Lv 1, Holy Lv 3, Dark Lv 5​

In the case above, transferring will result in:​

Transferor: Upgrade Lv 1, Holy Lv 2, Dark Lv 5​
Inheritor: Upgraded Lv 3, Holy Lv 3, Dark Lv 5​

A piece of gear that meets any of the requirements below can be selected as the transferor.​
・Upgrade Lv 1 or higher​
・Holy Lv 1 or higher​
・Dark Lv 1 or higher​
・Have 1 or more open rune slot​s

A piece of gear that meets the requirement below can be selected as the inheritor.​
・Possess at least 1 upgrade value that is a smaller number than the transferor's upgrade value.​

With Auto-Mount, you can automatically mount runes you have registered to premade custom sets.​
If you do not have enough runes or slots, the custom set will be mounted​

■STR​
The stat that affects P. DEF and ACC.​​
This is the unique type stat of Warriors, so high STR will give Warriors high ATK.​​
​
■DEX​​
The stat that affects EVD and CRIT.​​
This is the unique type stat of Snipers, so high DEX will give Snipers high ATK.​​
​
■MAG​​
The stat that affects M. DEF and Debuff ACC.​​
This is the unique type stat of Sorcerers, so high MAG will give Sorcerers high ATK.​​
​
■STA​​
The stat that affects HP and CRIT RES.​

■HP​
A character will be defeated if their HP drops to 0 in battle.​

■ATK​
The higher the number, the more damage is dealt.​

■DEF​
The higher the number, the less damage is taken.​

■DEF Break​
Deals damage by offsetting the damage reduction from the enemy's DEF.​

■SPD​
The higher the number, the easier it becomes to perform actions earlier.​

■P. DEF​
The higher the number, the less damage is taken from physical attacks.​
The basic attacks and skills of Warriors and Snipers are all physical attacks.​

■M. DEF​
The higher the number, the less damage is taken from magical attacks.​
The basic attacks and skills of Sorcerers are all magical attacks.​

■PM. DEF Break​
Deals damage by offsetting the damage reduction from the enemy's P. DEF and M. DEF.​

■ACC​
Raises an attack's chance to hit based on how high the number is.
Raising the chance to hit will raise the likelihood of success for an attack to hit.

■EVD​
Raises the chance to evade attacks based on how high the number is.
Raising the chance to evade will lower the chance to hit of attacks
directed at a character, and raise the likelihood of success for evading them.

■CRIT​
Raises the chance to deal a critical hit based on how high the number is.
Raising the chance to deal a critical hit will raise the likelihood of success
for a landed attack to become a critical hit.
When a critical hit is dealt, the amount of damage the attack deals increases.

■CRIT RES​
Raises the chance to resist a critical hit based on how the number is.
Raising the chance to resist a critical hit will lower the chance to deal a critical hit
of attacks taken by a character, and lower the likelihood of success
for those attacks to become critical hits.

■CRIT DMG Boost​
The higher the number, the higher the damage when dealing a critical hit.

■P. CRIT DMG Cut​
The higher the number, the less damage is taken
when an enemy's physical attack deals a critical hit.

■M. CRIT DMG Cut​
The higher the number, the less damage is taken
when an enemy's magical attack deals a critical hit.

■Debuff ACC​
Raises the chance to inflict a debuff based on how high the number is.​
Raising the chance to inflict a debuff will raise the likelihood of success
for the infliction of debuffs.

■Debuff RES​
Raises the chance to resist a debuff based on how high the number is.
Raising the chance to resist a debuff will lower the chance to inflict a debuff
of debuffs directed at a character, and lower the likelihood of success
for the infliction of those debuffs.

■Counter​
Deals damage to the enemy depending on the damage taken from them.​

■HP Drain​
Restores HP depending on the damage dealt to the enemy.​

■Lv Reset​
Spending Diamonds allows you to reset a character's Lv.​
The specified character's Lv will reset to 1,​
and all items used to level them up, as well gear they were equipping, will be returned.​

■Rarity Reset​
If you have 2 or more of the same character awakened to SSR or higher,​
a rarity reset can be performed on the one with a lower rarity.​

The designated character's rarity will reset to SR+,​
and all the characters used to awaken them, as well as gear they were equipping, will be returned.​
A character used for awakening will be returned as a Witch's Letter of the same Soul.​

Only a character with an initial rarity of SR can be reset.
A character with an initial rarity of R cannot be reset.

If the designated character's Lv is 2 or higher, a Lv Reset will also be performed.​

■Smelting​
By consuming D~A-rarity gear for smelting,​
you will have a chance to obtain gear with a rarity 1 level higher.​

By consuming S gear for smelting, you will have a chance to obtain dark gear.​
If dark gear could not be obtained, then you will obtain Fragments instead.​

If the smelted gear has already been upgraded, items used for upgrading will be returned.​
Gear with runes or Aug. Effects cannot be smelted.​

■Quick Battle​
Doing a Quick Battle allows you to obtain 2 hours worth of Auto-Battle rewards.​
The amount of rewards you can obtain will be based on your statistics at the time.​
Rewards will be sent to your Item Box.​

The number of Quick Battle attempts you can do in a day is limited.​
Having a higher VIP Lv will increase that number of attempts.​
Attempts will be reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​

Diamonds are required to do a Quick Battle, and the more attempts you do,​
the more Diamonds will be required.​
The required amount of Diamonds will be reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​

■Day Event​
Clearing designated main quests will unlock a Day Event.
While the Day Event is underway, Auto-Battle rewards will be increased.​

■Boss Battle
Emerging victorious in boss battles will give you rewards and unlock the next quest.
It will also allow you to Auto-Battle at the quest you just completed.

3 attempts can be made in a day for free, and attempts will reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).
Using Boss Tickets or Diamonds can restore your attempts.
Any amount of restored attempts that exceeds the max number for the day
will be carried over to the next day.

The number of attempts you can buy with Diamonds is limited,​
and the higher your VIP Lv is, the more attempts you will have.​
When you clear an uncleared quest, an attempt will not be used,
and even when you have 0 attempts left, you can still challenge uncleared quests.

■Battle Info​
You can check your Auto-Battle statistics here.​
The displayed numbers are used to determine the amounts of Auto-Battle rewards,​
Quick Battle rewards, and hourly item rewards you can obtain when the app is not in use.

■Population Info​
You can check the number of people you freed when clearing main quests here.​​
The amount of Gold and Kindling Orbs obtained from Auto-Battle rewards​​
depends on the number of people in your population.​​
As you clear certain main quests to free different countries, you can receive bonuses,​​
and you can check them all here.

■Battle League​
In Battle League, players battle each other to compete for rankings.​​
Select a randomly displayed opponent and battle.​​
​
If you win, the rankings of you and your opponent will be switched.​​
Defeating a player ranked lower than you will not change your ranking.​​
​
You can battle 5 times a day for free, and challenge attempts will be reset
every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​​
Diamonds can be spent to increase your attempts,
but they cannot be carried over into the next day.​​
​
If you win a battle you initiated, you can obtain victory rewards,​​
and if you lose you can obtain battle rewards.​​
Both victory and battle rewards will be sent to your Item Box.​​
​
If you are a player whose ranking is between 5~300,
your opponents will be displayed with their rankings hidden
​from 19:30~20:29 (Server Time) each day.

Additionally, you can obtain rewards based on your rankings as of 20:30 (Server Time) each day,​​
and the amount of rewards will increase as you rank higher.​​
These rewards will be sent to your Presents Box.​

■Legend League​
The Legend League is where high-ranking Battle League players from multiple Worlds​​
compete against each other for rankings.​​
​
■Commencement Periods/Seasons​
1 season takes place from Tuesday~Sunday.​
​
Ranking Calculation: Tuesday~Saturday 20:30 (Server Time)
Daily Battle Duration: 21:00~20:30 the next day (Server Time)​
​
■Participation Requirements​
Battle League results will be calculated daily while a season is underway,​
and players who fulfill the following requirements will be able to participate.​
​
・Having a Player Rank of 50 or higher​
・Being ranked in the top 50 of the Battle League at the time rankings are calculated​
​
Once a player participates in the Legend League,
even if they fall below the top 50 of the Battle League rankings mid-season,
they will still have their Points for the rest of the season,
and continue participating via defending only.​
​
■Challenge Attempts​
During a season, players who have fulfilled the participation requirements​
as of 20:30 (Server Time) each day will be granted 10 free challenge attempts.​
Diamonds can be spent to add up to 5 more challenge attempts.​​
Both free and purchased challenge attempts will be reset at 20:30 the next day (Server Time).​
​
■Points​
Players who have fulfilled the participation requirements mentioned above​
will be initially given 1000 Points,​
and the results of their battles will increase or decrease those Points as follows.​
​
・Win via attacking: +20 Points​
・Lose via attacking: +10 Points​
・Win via defending: No change in Points​
・Lose via defending: -10 Points​
​
If a player wins against an opponent who has 11 Points or more than them,
that player can obtain extra Points according to how large the difference is.

If a player initiates challenges, and goes on to have a win streak of 3 or more,
they can obtain extra Points according to the number of wins on their win streak.
*If the player is challenged and defeated by an opponent,
the win streak will come to an end.​
​
■Rankings​
Legend League rankings are sorted into two tabs: "Overall" and "World."​
Each tab can be viewed by tapping their respective button, which are found under Rankings.​
You can also find the "Previous" button there.
By tapping it, you can see the rankings of the previous season.
​
・Overall​
The players ranked in the top 50 of the season based on total Points are displayed here.​
​
・World​
The players ranked in the top 50 in the "Overall" tab who are from the same World as you,​
as well as their "Overall" ranking, are displayed here.​
​
■Rewards​
Players can tap the "Rewards" button to check the rewards they can obtain.​
Rewards are distributed to the Presents Box.​
​
・Daily Rewards​
These rewards are determined based on a player's ranking
as of 20:30 each day (Server Time) during the season.​
If a player has not fulfilled the participation requirements, they cannot claim these rewards.​
​
・Season Rewards​
These rewards are determined based on a player's ranking​
as of 20:30 on Sunday—the last day of the season (Server Time).​
​
・Icon Stamps
The number of Icon Stamps that can be obtained are determined based on a player's ranking
as of 20:30 each day (Server Time) during the season.
If a player has not fulfilled the participation requirements, they cannot collect any Icon Stamps.
By spending Icon Stamps, you can obtain Special Icons or Icon Effects.​

A player's class is determined based on their ranking and how many Points they have obtained.​
Additionally, the frame of a player's icon will automatically be changed​
depending on their current class.​
The requirements to reach each class are as follows.​

The higher rarity of a quest, the higher difficulty its requirements will be,
and the rewards you can obtain will be greater.

■Normal Quests
Only 1 of each of your characters can be dispatched to these quests.
Characters already dispatched to different normal quests cannot be selected.

Quests refresh every day at 4:00 (Server Time),
Any unaccepted quests at that time will be deleted, and new quests will be added.
You can spend Diamonds to refresh the available quests.

■Team Quests​
Your characters and those set as support characters by friends or guild members​
can be dispatched to these quests.​
Only 1 of each character can be dispatched to a quest.​
Characters already dispatched to different team quests cannot be selected.​
Characters already dispatched to normal quests or guerilla quests can be selected.​

New quests will be added every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​
Unaccepted quests will not be deleted.​

■Guerilla Quests​
Only your characters are dispatched to these quests.​
The times these quests appear change sporadically every day,
and a max of 1 quest will appear each day.​
Unlike other quests, there are no dispatch requirements,
and rewards will be greater based on the dispatched characters' rarities
and how unified their Souls are.

■Quick Finish
Spending Diamonds will allow you to instantly finish a quest.
The number of required Diamonds will depend on the time left before the quest is cleared.​

■Temple of Illusions
The Temple of Illusions allows you to team up with a max of 3 players and challenge bosses.
The Temple can be challenged at any time, 24 hours a day,
and you can obtain different rewards depending on the type of quest you clear.
If you create a team and do not start a battle after a certain period of time,
your team will be automatically disbanded.

The higher the difficulty, the more rewards you can obtain,
and you can challenge the Temple up to 6 times in 1 day.
Each quest has extra 1st try rewards exclusive to clearing the quest for the first time.
Additionally, you will earn boosted rewards by challenging the Temple between​
12:30~13:30 and 19:30~20:30 (Server Time).
The higher your Illusion Lv,
which rises in conjunction with the period of time that has passed since the opening of the World,
the stronger the quest bosses will be.

■Temple of Illusions Event​
While an event is underway, all the quests will turn into event quests,
and clearing them will allow you to obtain the special event item.
The special event item can be exchanged for rewards at the Shop.

■Tower of Infinity​
Defeating the enemies on each Floor will give you rewards and unlock the next Floor.​
3 attempts can be made in a day for free, and attempts will reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​

Using Tickets of Infinity or Diamonds can restore your attempts.
Any amount of restored attempts that exceeds the max number for the day
will be carried over to the next day.

The number of attempts you can buy with Diamonds is limited,​
and the higher your VIP Lv is, the more attempts you will have.​
When you clear an uncleared Floor, an attempt will not be used,​
and even when you have 0 attempts left, you can still challenge uncleared Floors.

■Tower of Souls​
The Towers of Azure, Crimson, Emerald, and Amber can be challenged
depending on the day of the week.
Characters can only enter if they have the Soul that matches the name of the tower.
Defeating the enemies on each Floor will give you rewards and unlock the next Floor.
Up to 10 Floors can be cleared in a day.

■Wish List
In your Wish List, you can set a max of 5 characters from each Soul, for a total of 20 characters.
The pull rates of the SR characters set in your Wish List will become higher.
The actual pull rates of all SR characters will not be changed.

If a total of 20 characters are set in all the slots, when an SR character is pulled,
one of those 20 characters or a character with a Soul of Radiance/Chaos will appear.
SR characters not set in the Wish List will no longer appear.
*In the Prayer of The Fleeting,
the featured character will appear regardless of how the Wish List is set.

Creating openings will not raise the pull rates of the other characters in your Wish List.

■Unlocking a Prayer of Souls​
As an option, you can spend Diamonds to unlock an additional Prayer of Souls.
The unlock period for the additional Prayer of Souls is 24 hours.
Only 1 additional Soul can be selected to unlock.​

■Guild Info
When guild members visit the Guild Info screen,
it allows them to obtain Guild EXP, Guild Stock, and Gold as a login bonus.
Collecting Guild EXP will raise the Guild Lv, and the max Lv a guild can reach is Lv 20.
Raising the Guild Lv will allow more guild members to join.
Additionally, the Guild Lv determines the limit on the amount of Guild EXP
a guild can obtain in a day.

■Guild Stock
Guild Stock is used to unlock Guild Raids, as well as participation qualifications for Guild Battles.
40 can be obtained from Quick Battles, 20 from winning boss battles,
10 from winning in the Battle League, and 40 from logging in to the guild.

A guild can hold no more than 70,000 in Guild Stock.
The obtainable amount, referred to as Guild Battle participation requirements,
will be added even after passing the limit.

■Roles​
There are four types of roles in guilds: Master, Chief, Commander, and Veterans.
Master: 1 Member​
Chief: Up to 1 Member​
Commander: Up to 3 Members​
Veterans: Unlimited​

If the amount of Guild Stock the Master has obtained in the past 3 days is 0,​
a new Master will be forcibly selected via the following order of priority.​
1. Chief
2. Commander​
3. Veterans​
4. Regular members​

If there are multiple members appointed to the role next in line to be the new Master,​
the one with the highest amount of Guild Stock in the past 7 days will be selected.

■Leaving
If you leave a guild, you can join a new guild 1 time on the same day.
But if you leave a second time, you cannot join a new guild until the next day at 4:00 (Server Time).

The Master cannot leave the guild.
For the Master to leave, they must appoint a different member as Master beforehand.

If a guild member leaves or is dismissed,
their Guild Stock from the past 7 days will continue to be displayed.

■Invitations
・Member Invitations
The Master and Chief can tap the "Approve" tab and find the "Member Invitations" button.
From there, the Master can search for players and invite them to join the guild.
Players can be searched for either by entering a Player ID,
or by tapping the "Settings" button to set conditions in the Search Settings screen.
The Master can also invite a player from their Player Profile by tapping the "Invite to Guild" button there.
Invitations can be sent to up to 20 players at once.
Players who have not unlocked the Guild feature cannot be invited to join a guild.

・Guild Invitations
Players who have received invitations can tap the "Guild Invitations" button on the Home screen,
as well as the "Invitations" button on the Join Guild screen.
After doing so, they can see a list of the guilds who have sent invitations,
as well as join/apply to join one of those guilds.
Players can change the conditions that determine which guilds can send them invitations
by tapping the "Settings" button and going to the Guild Invitations Settings screen.
A player can join a guild even if they do not meet that guild's BP requirement
only if the player has been invited by the guild.
A player can receive invitations from up to 20 guilds at once.
If a player is already a member of a guild, they cannot join/apply to join a new guild
until they leave their current one first.

■Guild Battle
Guilds in the previous day's top 16 of the Guild Stock Ranking can participate in Guild Battle.

■Calculating Period
In the following time period, the Guild Stock that guild members have collected will be calculated,
and that will determine the World’s Guild Stock Ranking.
・4:00 of the previous day~3:59 of the current day (Server Time)

■When the Participation Requirement Has Been Fulfilled
When a guild has fulfilled the requirement to participate in Guild Battle,
it will earn the right to [Declare] attacks on bases during Strategy Time on the current day.
Once it becomes War Phase, guilds will be able to [Siege] bases they [Declared] to attack.

*Please refer to Help on the Guild Battle screen for more details on Guild Battle.

■Guild Raid​
In Guild Raids, guild members join together to battle a boss,​
and can obtain rewards based on the amount of damage dealt.​
When the boss takes certain amounts of damage, their HP will increase,​
and the rewards will be even greater.​

On top of personal rewards, you obtain guild rewards based on the total damage dealt by all guild members.​
Guild rewards will be sent to your Presents Box.​
Members who do not participate in a Guild Raid cannot obtain any rewards.​

You cannot challenge a Guild Raid until 24 hours have passed after joining a guild.​
Additionally, if you leave a guild in the middle of a Guild Raid before claiming any rewards,​
you can no longer claim them unless you rejoin the guild by the time rewards are distributed.​

■Guild Boss​
The bosses who appear in Guild Raids are [Sonya] and [Luke].​
You can obtain 50 Guild EXP only when you challenge each of them for the first time.​
*Reaping also counts for the above.​

[Sonya] can be challenged 2 times a day,​
and the attempts will reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).​

[Luke] can be unlocked by spending 10,000 Guild Stock,​
and can be challenged 2 times whenever she is unlocked.​
Only the Master, Chief, Commander, and Veterans can unlock her.​
In addition, you cannot challenge Luke until 24 hours have passed​
since you have joined a guild.​

■Guild Raid Event
While an event is underway, a limited raid boss will appear,
and challenging them will allow you to obtain the special event item.
The special event item can be exchanged for rewards at the Shop.
Guild Stock is not required to unlock the limited-time raid boss,
as they can be challenged every day of the event by just using challenge attempts.

■World Rewards
These special rewards can be obtained according to the cumulative amount of damage
that every player in your World has dealt to the limited-time raid boss.

■Guild Battle​
In Guild Battles, several guilds fight for bases on the map.
Guilds in the previous day's top 16 of the Guild Stock Ranking can participate in Guild Battle.

■Event Times
Strategy Phase: 7:45~20:30 (Server Time)
War Phase: 20:45~21:30 (Server Time)
For Worlds where the Grand Battle will be commenced,​
the Guild Battle will be put on hiatus from Monday~Sunday on the week of the Grand Battle.​

After the Grand Battle ends, the Guild Battle will recommence, continuing from how
the status of​ the map, base ownership, etc., were before the hiatus started.​

■The Flow of Guild Battle
Guild Battles are composed of 2 phases: Strategy Phase and War Phase.

During Strategy Phase, you [Declare] attacks on red-colored bases.
When doing so, you can also deploy defense parties to your green-colored bases.

Once War Phase begins, you will [Siege] bases you have [Declared] to attack.
When all enemy defense parties are defeated, you can capture their base.

When War Phase ends, if there is at least 1 defense party, they can defend a base.
Regardless if it is Strategy Phase or War Phase, you can deploy a defense party to
defend your guild's bases.

A character who is already deployed cannot be deployed into a different party.
If you are in control of bases, but fall out of the top 16 of the Guild Stock Ranking,
you will no longer be able to siege. However, you will still be able to defend.
Furthermore, you cannot participate in the Guild Battle on the day you join a guild.

■Characters
Characters' stats and their equipped gear will be set at 20:30 (Server Time).​
From that point, any stat changes from leveling up, etc., will not be applied to the Guild Battle.

For both [Siege] and [Defend], each player can deploy only 1 of each character.
If you have duplicates of the same character in your roster,
the one with the highest BP will automatically be selected.

■Bases
There are 3 types of bases—churches, castles, and temples.
Rewards will differ depending on the type of base.
Small bases (churches) yield the fewest rewards, medium bases (castles) yield a moderate amount,
and large bases (temples) yield the most.
The minimum number of characters required for 1 party to be dispatched to a base
differs depending on the type of base.
The minimum number of characters required for 1 party will be increased
in conjunction with the period of time that has passed since the opening of the World.
The current minimum number of characters required for 1 party are as follows.

Temples: {0}
Castles: {1}
Churches: {2}

■Stamina
Each character has 2 points of stamina,
and using 1 point of stamina allows them to be deployed in a siege party of defense party.
When they run out of stamina, they can no longer be deployed.​
Deployed parties and stamina reset every day at 4:00 (Server Time).

■Declare
If there is a base you want to attack, select [Declare] during Strategy Phase.
Attacks can be declared on up to 2 bases in a day.
Bases that can be declared attack on are marked in red,
and can only be bases that are adjacent to your guild's.
You cannot declare attack on a base that has already been declared attack on by another guild.

Additionally, to declare attacks on castles and temples, the following requirements must be met.
・Temples: Have control of at least 1 castle.
・Castles: Have control of at least 2 churches, or 1 temple.

Guilds that have control of no bases can declare attacks on any church.
Only the Master, Chief, Commander, and Veterans can declare attacks.

■Siege
If you [Declared] attacks on bases during Strategy Phase, you can [Siege] them during War Phase.
By deploying a siege party to the target base, you can start a war,
and if all enemy defense parties are defeated, you can capture that base.

■War
A war consists of battles that occur at a base until a guild's deployed parties are defeated.
During a war, even if the enemy party is completely destroyed, your party’s HP will not be reset,
and they will continue to fight with the state of their HP carried over.
Furthermore, any temporary buffs and debuffs received during a battle will be dispelled
at the end of the battle.
If any skills have entered their skill cooldown times during a battle,
those skill cooldown times will be reset at the end of the battle.
However, if a character has a skill with "This skill activates only 1 time per battle"
written in its description, unless specified otherwise, that skill will activate only 1 time
while the character is engaged in consecutive battles.

During the war, siege parties will be enhanced with [Guild Battle Buffs].
SPD will be increased, and the buffs’ effects will become smaller the more battles are won.
Those buffs will remain until that party is defeated.

The winning party will be inflicted with [Guild Battle Debuffs] based on
the number of enemies defeated.
The more battles a party wins, the greater the effects of the [Guild Battle Debuffs] will become,​
with the effects lasting until that party is defeated.

The K.O. animation will automatically change based on
the Legend League and Battle League Rankings of the winning player.

■Defense
You can deploy a defense party to your bases to protect them.
These bases are marked in green on the map.
Defense parties can be deployed regardless if it is Strategy Phase or War Phase.
Characters deployed in a defense party cannot be deployed to another base
until their party is defeated.
The deployment of defense parties resets every day at 4:00 (Server Time).

■Counter
[Counter] can be selected if it is within 15 minutes after a base is captured.
If [Counter] is selected, the counter will begin 15 minutes after the base was captured.

When countering, defenders and attackers will switch roles,
and the sieging guild will deploy a defense party, while the defending guild deploys a siege party.
The siege party that was deployed when sieging a base will remain deployed there as a defense party.
The defense party that was deployed to the base, but was defeated, can take back the base.
Only the Master, Chief, Commander, and Veterans can counter.

​■Base Memos​
You can set Marks and Messages at your bases that can only be read by other guild members.​
Only bases that have met the following conditions can have Base Memos set.​
・Bases your guild can declare attacks or counters on​​
・Bases your guild has control of
Any Base Memos set will be automatically deleted after the War Phase has ended.​
Only the Master, Chief, and Commander can edit Base Memos.​

■Rewards
Rewards can be obtained from the Guild Info screen.
・Qualified Guilds: Guilds who have control of a base as of 4:00 (Server Time)
・Reward Claiming Period: 4:00~3:59 the next day (Server Time)
・Who can Claim Rewards: Guild members who have joined a qualified guild
before the reward claiming period starts.

You can check any base's rewards from their Base Info screen.
Any rewards left unclaimed when the reward claiming period ends will be discarded.​
During the Guild Battle hiatus period, rewards can still be claimed based on the results​
of the Guild Battle that took place on the day before the hiatus period.​
Rewards will depend on the number and types of bases a guild has control of.

■MVP​
The MVPs of the Guild Battle will be displayed here.​
There are two categories for MVP, Siege and Defense,​
and the top 3 players in each category will be displayed.​
The MVP ranking calculations will be reset at 21:31 (Server Time),​
and the top 3 players in both categories of that day's Guild Battle will be displayed.​
*For the duration that MVPs are displayed,​
if a guild changes their name, or if any players leave a guild,​
the information displayed will still reflect the time the MVP rankings were calculated.​

MVP Ranking Calculation: 21:30 (Server Time)​
MVP Display Duration: 21:31~21:30 of the next day (Server Time)​
